## 6. Authoring conventions

A conformant DSL follows these conventions:

1. **Names**: SwiftUI view/modifier names; per-language case (camelCase,
   snake_case). `foregroundStyle` not `foregroundColor`; `fontWeight`,
   `multilineTextAlignment`, `scaledToFit`, `allowsHitTesting` keep their
   SwiftUI spellings. A modifier's type is **never** suffixed `Mod`.
2. **Signature order**: canonical parameter order is preserved —
   `.border(color, width)`, `.frame(width, height, alignment)`,
   `.shadow(color, radius, x, y)`. Compound modifiers expand to one property
   per argument.
3. **Values vs modifiers**: structural/layout values and a control's bound value
   are configured through `with(...)`; everything else is a chainable
   `modifiers(...)` value. The three operations may be chained in any order.
4. **Typed enums**: `HorizontalAlignment` (leading/center/trailing, for
   `VStack`), `VerticalAlignment` (top/center/bottom, for `HStack`), `Alignment`
   (2D — topLeading … bottomTrailing — for `ZStack`/grids and the `frame`
   modifier's content alignment); all **position-only, never stretching** (a
   child's `FILL` size kind stretches). Plus `TextAlignment`, `FontWeight`
   (100–900), `Truncation` (head/middle/tail),
   `TextCase` (none/uppercase/lowercase), `FontStyle` (normal/italic),
   `FontDesign` (default/serif/rounded/monospaced), `ContentMode` (fit/fill),
   `ControlSize` (small/regular/large), `ToggleStyle`
   (switch/checkbox/button), `PickerStyle` (menu/segmented/wheel/radiogroup),
   `DatePickerMode` (date/time/dateAndTime), `ShapeKind`
   (circle/rectangle/roundedRectangle/capsule/ellipse/path). Numeric codes
   come from MODIFIERS.md's appendix; the DSL resolves them.
5. **`Spacer`/`Color` as views**: `Spacer` is a flexible expanding filler;
   `Color` in a tree is a layout-greedy fill.
6. **The environment is the only inheritance mechanism.** Any value that must
   reach a whole subtree — a style (`ButtonStyle`), the router, the active path,
   the session's persisted state — is injected through the environment, never
   threaded through constructors and never through a second scoping system. The
   environment is a hierarchical, nearest-wins scope of typed `EnvironmentKey`
   values (the `EnvironmentBinding` modifier value / `Environment.value(key)`,
   Java; §4.5). A language MAY implement the scope with a thread-local over the
   synchronous render pass (Java does) — but that is the implementation of the
   one mechanism, not an additional one. A subtree-scoping modifier MUST be
   expressed as an `EnvironmentKey` binding: `ButtonStyle` binds
   `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE` (`EnvironmentKey<ButtonStyle>`), exactly like the
   router and the active path.
7. **Reactivity discipline**: `body()` is evaluated once; a signal read during
   mount records a dependency; a later write re-emits only the bound node.
   Never mutate signals during mount. The only structural re-evaluation is a
   structural container ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)),
   which the emitter reconciles into `TREE` deltas.
8. **Emission contract**: each DSL call emits exactly the documented
   properties with the documented value types; the emitter diffs. The DSL never
   computes layout, never positions, never serializes full trees.

## 7. Theme management

Pathland theming is **application-owned over a renderer-owned token system**
([TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md); the wire encoding lives in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md)
§Design Token System). The DSL gives the author two distinct surfaces:

1. **Token references in style modifiers** — semantic intent instead of a
   literal: `ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(Color.token("color.primary")))`
   emits a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference the renderer resolves against the current
   scheme. No opcode is re-emitted when a token or the scheme changes.
2. **Global theme overrides** — a batch of `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` commands
   rolled at mount: a single-scheme `Theme` or an `AdaptiveTheme` light+dark
   pair (base = **light**, `dark.`-prefixed = **dark**).

> **Ownership**: the application owns theme values (base + `dark.*`) and token
> references; the renderer owns token defaults (light + dark), effective
> color-scheme detection, resolution (override → default → parent → fallback),
> and interaction-state styling (hover/pressed/focus/disabled). The protocol
> never transmits hover/click/transition styling.

### 7.1 Token-typed values

Any property whose value type is `COLOR` / `F32` / `STRING` / `ENUM` MAY carry a
**token reference** instead of a literal value (MODIFIERS.md §Value types). The
reference rides the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (`0x08`) with the token path in
the arena — **never** a packed literal. A property carries exactly one value
(literal or reference, never both).

| Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Rust DSL | Emits |
|----------------------------|----------|----------|-------|
| `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color.token("color.primary")` | `Color::token("color.primary")` | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref (`0x08`) in any COLOR-typed property: `COLOR` 0x100A (`.foregroundStyle`), `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001, `BORDER_COLOR` 0x1004, `SHADOW_COLOR` 0x1021, `TINT` 0x1030, … |
| `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color.token("dark.color.surface")` | `Color::token("dark.color.surface")` | same — an explicit dark-variant reference |
| `.padding(space.2)` / `Spacing(space.2)` | (token-valued spacing/padding) | (token-valued spacing/padding) | `DESIGN_TOKEN` ref in a F32-typed property: `PADDING` 0x1011 / `SPACING` 0x0001 / `CONTENT_MARGINS` 0x0005, … (see TOKENS.md §Generative token families) |

`Color` keeps its dual identity: as a **View** it is a layout-greedy fill; as a
token reference (`Color.token(path)`) it is a **data value** passed to
style-taking modifiers. A token-typed property resolves renderer-side and
**re-resolves automatically** when the effective scheme changes — overrides and
scheme are renderer state, so no node is ever re-emitted for a theme/scheme
change.

Rules:

1. Reference any token path — the standard catalog (TOKENS.md §Standard Token
   Catalog) or an application-defined path. A renderer that cannot apply a token
   falls back rather than erroring.
2. `space.<N>` members are **generative**: reference them freely (`space.2`,
   `space.0.5`), but override only `space.base` (see §7.2 rule 2).
3. A token reference must not be combined with a literal on the same property.

### 7.2 Global theme overrides

A **theme** is a batch of token overrides. Every override defines **exactly one
value**; combine a light and a dark `Theme` via `AdaptiveTheme` for adaptive
theming.

| Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view` / `pathland-engine`) | Emits |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|
| `Theme()` — one-scheme override batch | `Theme.with()` / `ThemeData` | `Theme::new()` | one `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` per override (`A` = arena path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value) |
| `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `.color("color.primary", 0xFF2563EB)` | `COLOR`-typed override (sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`) |
| `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0f)` | `.f32("space.base", 4.0)` | `F32`-typed override (lengths in device pixels) |
| `.u32("…", v)` / `.u8("…", v)` | `.u32(path, int)` / `.u8(path, int)` | `.u32(path, v)` / `.u8(path, v)` | `U32` / `U8`-typed override |
| `.string("font.body.family", "Inter")` | `.string(path, String)` | `.string(path, "Inter")` | `STRING`-typed override (arena) |
| `AdaptiveTheme(light, dark)` | `AdaptiveTheme.with(light, dark)` | `AdaptiveTheme::new(light, dark)` | light overrides as base tokens; dark overrides `dark.`-prefixed |

Emission contract:

- The theme is emitted **once at mount** as a frame of
  `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes before the tree. Java: `new Emitter(sink,
  theme)` emits it at the start of the mount and `renderFull` (resync) frames;
  Rust: `Engine::apply_theme` / `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme`.
- Overrides are **renderer state**: they never re-emit nodes and never
  participate in the diff — an unchanged tree with a theme still emits **zero**
  per-node opcodes.
- `AdaptiveTheme` emits the light `Theme`'s overrides as base paths and the dark
  `Theme`'s with the `dark.` prefix (added automatically when the author wrote a
  bare path). The renderer derives the effective scheme from the platform and
  resolves each override against it.
- The renderer supplies light + dark defaults for the whole Tier 1 catalog, so
  dark mode works even when the author only overrides base tokens.

Authoring rules:

1. Override any token in the catalog or an application-defined path; never
   assume specific renderer default values.
2. Override `space.base` to control the whole spacing scale — individual
   `space.<N>` members MUST NOT be overridden.
3. Overrides are **global and renderer-wide**: apply the theme once per
   session/host at mount, not per view.

## 8. Java DSL convergence (adopted)

The Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) has the complete surface. The convergence
below has been **adopted**: construction through the three operations
(`with` / `modifiers` / `children`), and modifiers as `ViewModifier` values with
**no `Mod` suffix** and **no per-modifier sugar on `View`**. The canonical
contract is [§4](#4-view-surface) and [§5](#5-modifier-surface).

| Canonical | Java (adopted) | Optional / remaining |
|-----------|----------------|----------------------|
| `Text("…")` | `Text.with(t -> t.text("…"))` (String or `Signal<String>`) | — |
| `Button("…", action)` / `Button(action:label:)` | `Button.with(b -> b.title("…").action(action))` and/or `.children(label)` | — |
| `Toggle("label", isOn: writable)` | `Toggle.with(t -> t.label("…").isOn(writable))` | — |
| `Slider(value: in:)` | `Slider.with(s -> s.value(writable).min(..).max(..))` (binding in config) | — |
| `.border(color, width)` | `Border.with(b -> b.color(..).width(..))` via `.modifiers(...)` | radius convenience on the same builder |
| `DatePicker(selection:)` | `DatePicker.with(d -> d.mode(..).selection(days))` | *optional* `Date`-shaped config encoding days + millis-of-day per `SET_DATE`/`DATE_CHANGED` |

Adopted conventions:

- **`with` / `modifiers` / `children` are the one construction path.** Every
  concrete view/control exposes these three operations; `.of(...)` is gone.
  They are available **at creation or chained, in any order**
  ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)).
- **`with(config)` is a fluent config builder.** The config holds the view's
  values and is the same type a style's `makeBody(Config)` reads
  ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
- **The `View.*` static-factory surface is removed.** The entire factory block
  (`text`, `image`, `rectangle`, `spacer`, `vstack`, `hstack`, `zstack`,
  `button`, `textField`, `textEditor`, `toggle`, `slider`, `stepper`,
  `progressView`, `gauge`, `divider`, `grid`, `scrollView`, `lazyVStack`,
  `lazyHStack`, `lazyVGrid`, `lazyHGrid`, `picker`, `menu`, `colorPicker`,
  `datePicker`, `group`) is deleted from `View.java`.
- **`Group` is a first-class view.** `Group.with().children(View...)` is a
  transparent container view (SwiftUI `Group`).
- **Core and custom modifiers share one mechanism.** Core modifiers are
  `ViewModifier` values (`Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))`,
  `ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(color))`) applied via `.modifiers(...)` —
  there is **no sugar on `View`**; several modifiers at once use
  `.modifiers(...)`, innermost-first. Single-value modifiers pass the value
  directly (`FontWeight.BOLD`).
- **No `Mod` suffix.** A modifier type is named for the modifier it applies;
  where it wraps a single value, the value type is the modifier. Main's
  `FrameMod → Frame` (with the wire batch renamed `emit.Frame → ProtocolFrame`)
  is the precedent; the remaining `*Mod` types are renamed accordingly
  (`FontWeightMod → FontWeight`, `ButtonStyleMod → ButtonStyle`, …;
  `EnvironmentMod → EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod → NavigationIntent`).
- **Full `ShapeKind` coverage.** `Circle.with()`, `Capsule.with()`,
  `Ellipse.with()`, `RoundedRectangle.with(r -> r.cornerRadius(..))`, generic
  `Shape.with(s -> s.kind(ShapeKind))` (for `Path`).
- Implementation status: `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md`.

## 9. Generation contract for a new language

An AI (or a human) generating a Pathland DSL in a new language MUST produce the
following and verify each item. This is a checklist; the authoritative details
are the companion specs.

### 9.1 Required surface

- [ ] **Views/controls** — every entry of [§4](#4-view-surface):
  `Text`, `Image`, `Color`, `Shape` (all `ShapeKind`s), `Divider`, `Spacer`,
  `ProgressView`, `Gauge`; `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`,
  `ScrollView`,
  `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`; `Button`,
  `TextField`, `SecureField`, `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`,
  `Picker`, `Menu`, `DatePicker`, `ColorPicker`.
- [ ] **The three operations** — configure values, apply modifiers, supply
  children — available at creation or by chaining, in any order
  ([§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)). Each language maps them to its idiom
  ([§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)).
- [ ] **Modifiers** — every entry of [§5](#5-modifier-surface), applicable to
  any view, innermost-first, emitting one property per underlying argument; a
  modifier's type carries no `Mod` suffix.
- [ ] **Custom modifiers / unified mechanism** — a `ViewModifier` authoring
  surface (`body(content) -> View`) + a chainable `modifiers(...)` operation on
  **any** view; **core modifiers are implemented through the same mechanism**,
  never a separate syntax ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
- [ ] **Shared config with styles** — a style's `makeBody(Config)` receives the
  same config type the control configured via `with(...)`
  ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
- [ ] **Signals** — `signal`, `computed`, `effect`, `untracked`,
  `get`/`set`/`update`/`asReadonly`, with equality suppression, synchronous
  flush, glitch-free propagation, error caching, write discipline, circular
  detection ([§3.1](#31-signal-surface)).
- [ ] **Two-way bindings** — every value control takes a writable signal (a
  config value) and exposes a sink the host routes its event into
  ([§3.2](#32-two-way-binding)).
- [ ] **Persisted state** — `State<T>` keyed fields (or the language's
  equivalent wiring) against a platform-neutral store ([§3.3](#33-persisted-state-statet)).
- [ ] **Gestures** — `.onTapGesture` (composed from raw pointer down/up) and
  raw `pointerEvents`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` bitmask ([§4.4](#44-gestures)).
- [ ] **Structural reactivity (conditional rendering)** — a structural
  container over a selector signal (`Conditional.when(...)` / `Case.of` /
  `Case.otherwise`, or the language's `if`/`switch` equivalent), reconciling
  the slot into `TREE` deltas with zero opcodes for identical structure
  ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)).
- [ ] **Navigation** — `Router` / `RouteTable` / `NavigationContainer` /
  `NavigationLink` over a plain `Signal<Route>`, the initial route host-seeded
  before mount, emitting `ROUTE` and `TRANSITION` and consuming the `NAVIGATE`
  event ([§4.5](#45-navigation)).
- [ ] **Design tokens & theming** — a token surface: token-typed values usable
  in style modifiers (a `Color` accepting a token path, e.g. `Color.token("color.primary")`
  or the language's equivalent), a theme/override helper emitting
  `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (base values + `dark.`-prefixed dark values), and
  the **base=light / `dark.*`** color-scheme convention with renderer-derived
  scheme detection — see [§7](#7-theme-management) and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md).

### 9.2 Mapping rules (signature → protocol)

1. Each view/control maps to its **fixed component id** in PRIMITIVES.md.
   Application/custom component types live in `0x0100`–`0xFFFF`; a DSL must
   never reuse allocated ids.
2. Each modifier maps to the **documented property id(s)** in MODIFIERS.md
   with the documented **value type** (U8/U32/I32/F32/STRING/ENUM/COLOR/
   DESIGN_TOKEN). Enumerated values use the numeric codes in MODIFIERS.md's
   appendix.
3. `Color` values pack as sRGB `0xAARRGGBB`. A **token-typed** value instead
   carries the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type with the token path in the arena
   (never a packed literal); the renderer resolves it against the current
   scheme. A theme/override helper emits `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`
   (`A` = arenaRef path, `B` = valueType, `C` = value); a `dark.`-prefixed path
   supplies the dark design (base = light — [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
4. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` sentinels: `FILL` = −1.0, `HUG_CONTENT` = −2.0.
5. `Grid` counts map to the **config values** `GRID_COLUMNS` (`0x001E`) /
   `GRID_ROWS` (`0x001F`): a positive `int` count emits a positive F32; absent =
   auto-fit. A **`List<GridItem>`** value serializes to the **`GRID_TRACKS`**
   (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track spec, which takes precedence over the counts. A
   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` frame on a grid is the grid's **box**, never a count
   ([§4.2](#42-layout--container-nodes)).
6. `DatePicker` value/event use the two-field encoding **days since epoch
   (I32) + millis of day (U32)**; there is no `DATE_VALUE` property.
7. Value/text/date events are gated by the transport-aware event guards; the
   DSL's controls emit the `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS` that
   declare intent.
8. Emission is **diff-based and reactive**: the DSL describes values, the
   emitter diffs. A generated DSL must keep the retained tree + emitter
   separation; it must not hand-serialize full trees.

### 9.3 Language adaptation rules

**The three operations are normative; their spellings are not.** A conformant
DSL MUST expose *configure values*, *apply modifiers*, and *supply children*,
each available at creation or by chaining (any order), mapped to the host
language's idioms. The canonical (Java/SwiftUI-shaped) spelling is
`with` / `modifiers` / `children`.

| Aspect | Java | C# | Rust | Go | Python |
|--------|------|----|------|----|--------|
| configure values | `with(c -> …)` | `With(c => …)` | `with(\|c\| …)` | ctor + options | kwargs / `configure(…)` |
| apply modifiers | `.modifiers(…)` | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers([…])` | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` |
| supply children | `.children(…)` | `.Children(…)` | `.children([…])` / `vstack![…]` | ctor args / `.Children(…)` | `.children(*v)` |
| creation + chaining | static on the view; chain on the returned builder | static on the view; chain via **extension methods** | associated fn `Type::with`; chain via a **trait** + macros | package ctor; chain via methods | kwargs + methods |
| same-name static + chain | **builder split** (static on class, chain on builder) | extension methods (separate static class) | assoc fn + trait method | package func + method (not type-scoped) | **not expressible** (methods are last-wins) |
| `with` name legal | yes | yes (`With`; lowercase `with` is the record keyword) | yes | yes | **no** — `with` is a keyword → kwargs / `configure` |
| varargs children | yes | `params` | no — slices/arrays or macros | `...` | `*args` |
| value *is* the modifier | enum OK | **enum can't implement an interface** → `record struct` / static readonly value | enum OK | typed const + method OK | enum member with `apply` OK |

Rules:

- A language that cannot express "static-or-chained under one name" (Python)
  MUST still offer the three operations — value configuration via kwargs /
  `configure(...)`, modifiers and children via chainable methods.
- A language whose enums cannot implement the modifier interface (C#) MUST
  supply the equivalent single-value modifier form (a `record struct`, a static
  readonly value, or an implicit conversion).
- Names are recommendations; semantics
  ([§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)) are the contract.

### 9.4 Conformance recipe

A generated DSL is verified by proving it **emits the same bytes** as the
reference implementations:

1. Port the golden vectors in [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) into the new
   DSL's test harness; assert byte-identical `TREE`/`PARAMETER`/`EVENT`/`META`
   opcodes for each canonical element.
2. Port the Java `EmitterTest` cases (mount → `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE`
   deltas; unchanged tree → zero opcodes; two-way routing: `TEXT_CHANGED`,
   `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED` write into the bound signal).
3. Verify the no-heap-allocation steady-state property where the target
   language supports it (the Rust engine proves zero dynamic allocations during
   steady-state emission).
4. Cross-check every referenced id against PRIMITIVES.md/MODIFIERS.md/EVENTS.md
   (the specs are the source of truth, never the reference code).

**Reference implementations to read**: Java — `lib/java/pathland-view`
(`com.pathland.view`, `com.pathland.view.signal`, `com.pathland.view.state`,
`com.pathland.view.emit`); Rust — `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view` +
`pathland-engine` + `pathland-core::signal`.

- The wire footprint of every DSL element above is defined by the golden

- The v2 authoring surface (`with` / `modifiers` / `children`, shared

148: ### The three operations
149: 
150: Every concrete view exposes the same three operations. They form one fluent
151: **builder**: any of the three may be the first call, and they may be chained in
152: any order. A later call overrides an earlier value for the same property.
153: 
154: | Operation | Purpose | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) |
155: |-----------|---------|----------------------------|
156: | **values** | Configure structural/layout values and a control's bound value | `View(config:)` — labels in the constructor |
157: | **modifiers** | Apply `ViewModifier` values, innermost-first | `.modifier(_:)` / `.padding(_:)` / … |
158: | **children** | Supply the content subtree (content-bearing views only) | trailing closure `{ … }` |
159: 
160: The **canonical builder spelling** (the recommended form; per-language spellings
161: are in [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)) is:
162: 
163: ```
164: ViewName.with { values }              // values   — a config-builder lambda
165:       .modifiers(modifier, ...)       // modifiers — varargs
166:       .children(view, ...)            // children  — varargs, content-bearing views only
167: ```
168: 
169: Any of the three may start the chain, e.g. all of these are equivalent:
170: 
171: ```
172: VStack.with { v in v.spacing(8) }.children(a, b).modifiers(m)
173: VStack.children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }.modifiers(m)
174: VStack.modifiers(m).children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }
175: ```
176: 
177: **Values are a config-builder lambda.** `with { c in … }` populates a per-view
178: fluent **config** (`VStack.Config`, `Text.Config`, …). The config accepts raw
179: values **or** `Signal`s (so `c.text(signal)` stays reactive) and is the *same
180: type* a style's `makeBody(Config)` receives ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
181: The builder is **fluent and mutable**: setters return the config. Config-less
182: views (`Divider`, `Spacer`) take an empty `with()`.
183: 
184: **Per-language realization.** Java cannot declare a static and an instance
185: method with the same signature, so the Java realization holds the three
186: statically on the view class and exposes the chainable forms on the returned
187: builder/view type. Other languages map the operations to their idioms
188: (extension methods, associated functions + traits, package constructors +
189: methods, kwargs) — see [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).
190: 
191: Per-language adaptation summary:
192: 
193: | Language | Case | Composition mechanism | Example |
194: |----------|------|-----------------------|---------|
195: | SwiftUI | `camelCase` | trailing closures + result builder | `VStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 8) { Text("x").padding(16) }` |
196: | Java (`com.pathland.view`) | `camelCase` | `with(Consumer)` builder + `modifiers(...)` + `children(...)` | `VStack.with(v -> v.spacing(8)).children(Text.with(t -> t.text("x")).modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))))` |
197: | Rust (`pathland-view`) | `snake_case` | assoc fn + `ViewExt` trait + macros | `vstack![text("x").modifiers([Padding(16.0)])]` |

1261: ### 9.3 Language adaptation rules
1262: 
1263: **The three operations are normative; their spellings are not.** A conformant
1264: DSL MUST expose *configure values*, *apply modifiers*, and *supply children*,
1265: each available at creation or by chaining (any order), mapped to the host
1266: language's idioms. The canonical (Java/SwiftUI-shaped) spelling is
1267: `with` / `modifiers` / `children`.
1268: 
1269: | Aspect | Java | C# | Rust | Go | Python |
1270: |--------|------|----|------|----|--------|
1271: | configure values | `with(c -> …)` | `With(c => …)` | `with(\|c\| …)` | ctor + options | kwargs / `configure(…)` |
1272: | apply modifiers | `.modifiers(…)` | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers([…])` | `.Modifiers(…)` | `.modifiers(…)` |
1273: | supply children | `.children(…)` | `.Children(…)` | `.children([…])` / `vstack![…]` | ctor args / `.Children(…)` | `.children(*v)` |
1274: | creation + chaining | static on the view; chain on the returned builder | static on the view; chain via **extension methods** | associated fn `Type::with`; chain via a **trait** + macros | package ctor; chain via methods | kwargs + methods |
1275: | same-name static + chain | **builder split** (static on class, chain on builder) | extension methods (separate static class) | assoc fn + trait method | package func + method (not type-scoped) | **not expressible** (methods are last-wins) |
1276: | `with` name legal | yes | yes (`With`; lowercase `with` is the record keyword) | yes | yes | **no** — `with` is a keyword → kwargs / `configure` |
1277: | varargs children | yes | `params` | no — slices/arrays or macros | `...` | `*args` |
1278: | value *is* the modifier | enum OK | **enum can't implement an interface** → `record struct` / static readonly value | enum OK | typed const + method OK | enum member with `apply` OK |
1279: 
1280: Rules:
1281: 
1282: - A language that cannot express "static-or-chained under one name" (Python)
1283:   MUST still offer the three operations — value configuration via kwargs /
1284:   `configure(...)`, modifiers and children via chainable methods.
1285: - A language whose enums cannot implement the modifier interface (C#) MUST
1286:   supply the equivalent single-value modifier form (a `record struct`, a static
1287:   readonly value, or an implicit conversion).
1288: - Names are recommendations; semantics
1289:   ([§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)) are the contract.
1290:

906:   `Environment.<name>Style()` accessor. This is the one inheritance mechanism
907:   ([§6 rule 6](#6-authoring-conventions)); `ButtonStyle` binds
908:   `Environment.BUTTON_STYLE`, `AudioStyle` `Environment.AUDIO_STYLE`,
909:   `VideoStyle` `Environment.VIDEO_STYLE`, `LabelStyle`
910:   `Environment.LABEL_STYLE`.
911: - **Button content precedence (three developer options).** A `Button`'s content
912:   resolves as: (1) an **explicit child** supplied via `.children(...)` wins;
913:   else (2) the config **title** string (wrapped as a `Text`); else (3) the
914:   **style-supplied content** from `makeBody`. The `buttonStyle` modifier itself
915:   (option 3) lets a developer hand content in through the style. This mirrors
916:   SwiftUI's multiple button-authoring forms.
917: - **Defaults preserve the native path.** The default style contributes the
918:   control's natural content: `PlainButtonStyle` → the label;
919:   `NativeAudioStyle`/`NativeVideoStyle` → **no content** (an empty-content
920:   sentinel), so the control stays a **leaf** in Native Token Mode and the
921:   renderer shows native media controls; `DefaultLabelStyle` → title + icon.
922: - **Text/foreground modifiers cascade to content.** A `.foregroundStyle`/
923:   `.fontSize` (and the other inherited text modifiers) applied *to the control*
924:   reach the content's text — SwiftUI environment semantics. In the Java DSL the
925:   properties ride the control node; renderers cascade them to child text.
926: - **Main-axis alignment is the content's own layout — no protocol property.**
927:   A control's content box centers its child by default; to left-align a
928:   composite label (e.g. a navigation row), make the label full-width
929:   (`Frame.with(f -> f.width(FILL))`) and let its own `ALIGNMENT` place its
930:   content. There is deliberately no main-axis/justification property (the engine
931:   describes WHAT, never WHERE — [§1](#1-design-principles-dsl-flavored)).
932: - **Closed-variant ("token") styles are the same surface, not a wrapper.** Some
933:   styles select a whole native variant rather than supplying content:
934:   `ToggleStyle`/`PickerStyle`/`TextStyle` are wire **enums** applied as
935:   properties (`TOGGLE_STYLE`, …), and `LabelStyle` shapes which parts render.
936:   They are scoped/read exactly like the wrapper styles above.
937: 
938: Canonical signatures (SwiftUI-shaped) and the realization:
939: 
940: | Control | Style protocol | `Config` | Default style |
941: |---------|----------------|----------|---------------|
942: | `Button` | `ButtonStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | the `Button.Config` (title, action, content) | `PlainButtonStyle` (label) |
943: | `Label` | `LabelStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | the `Label.Config` (title, icon) | `DefaultLabelStyle` (title + icon) |
944: | `Audio` | `AudioStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | the `Audio.Config` (playing, position, volume, duration) | `NativeAudioStyle` (no content) |
945: | `Video` | `VideoStyle { makeBody(config) -> View }` | the `Video.Config` (playing, position, volume, duration) | `NativeVideoStyle` (no content) |

949: enum MyButtonStyle implements ButtonStyle { INSTANCE;
950:     @Override public View makeBody(Button.Config c) {
951:         return c.content().modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(12)), Background.with(b -> b.color(BLUE)));
952:     }
953: }
954: Button.with(b -> b.title("Save").action(this::save)).modifiers(MyButtonStyle.INSTANCE);
955: 
956: // Label: the style decides which parts render (nullable parts = absent).
957: enum BadgeLabelStyle implements LabelStyle { INSTANCE;
958:     @Override public View makeBody(Label.Config c) {
959:         return HStack.with().children(
960:                 c.icon().modifiers(Frame.with(f -> f.width(18).height(18))),
961:                 c.title());
962:     }
963: }

1: //! # pathland-view
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,
4: //! `Text`) and chainable modifiers (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`,
5: //! `background`) build a retained **view tree** (`pathland_engine::Node`) that the
6: //! diff emitter in `pathland-core` turns into declarative `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes.
7: //!
8: //! ## Building a tree
9: //!
10: //! Use the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros (which box children for you) with the
11: //! free `text`/`spacer` functions, then chain modifiers and `build()`:
12: //!
13: //! ```
14: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, hstack, text, View, ViewExt};
15: //!
16: //! let node = vstack![
17: //!     text("a"),
18: //!     hstack![text("b")],
19: //! ]
20: //! .padding(16.0)
21: //! .build();
22: //! # let _ = node;
23: //! ```
24: //!
25: //! ## Decoupled modifiers
26: //!
27: //! Modifiers are **decoupled from views** (SwiftUI-style): any modifier applies
28: //! to any view via the blanket `View::modifier`, and application code composes
29: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:
30: //!
31: //! ```
32: //! use pathland_view::{View, ViewExt, ViewModifier, Node, Padding, Background, Color};
33: //!
34: //! struct Card;
35: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
36: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
37: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
38: //!         Background(Color::argb(0xFF_EEEEEE)).apply(node);
39: //!     }
40: //! }
41: //!
42: //! // Works on any view:
43: //! let a = pathland_view::text("A").with(Card);
44: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].with(Card);
45: //! # let _ = (a, b);
46: //! ```
47: //!
48: //! Unsupported combinations are **allowed and ignored**: the modifier emits its
49: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.
50: //!
51: //! ## No layout math
52: //!
53: //! The DSL describes structure + constraint properties only. It never computes
54: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.
55: //!
56: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`.
57:

94: ///
95: /// Each child is boxed automatically, so children can mix `Text`, `HStack`,
96: /// modified views, or custom `View` implementations. Nested stacks work:
97: ///
98: /// ```

100: /// let node = vstack![text("a"), text("b")].build();

2004: /// A `SizeThatFits` candidate: a view plus the minimum container width at which
2005: /// it is selected. The candidates' thresholds form the wire `FIT_QUERY` table

2007: /// locally, and reports `FIT_CHANGED` (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §SizeThatFits).

2019:     /// A candidate with threshold 0 — always applicable (the fallback).
2020:     pub fn any(view: impl View + 'static) -> Self {

# pathland-view (Rust DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 2, 2026

The SwiftUI-style **view DSL** (`no_std`) building `pathland_engine::Node`
trees. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Views**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`,
  `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`,
  `Icon` (semantic symbols via `IconName` + `icon(…)`), `Image`, `Color` (dual identity: a layout-greedy View *and* a value passed
  into style modifiers), `Shape`, `Divider`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`,
  `Toggle`, `Slider`, `TextField`, `TextEditor`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`,
  `Picker`, `Menu`, `ColorPicker` (+ the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros and
  `text`/`spacer`/`button` free functions).
- **Modifiers** (chainable, decoupled): `spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`,
  `font_weight`, `font(Font)`, `font_family(&str)`, `font_design(FontDesign)`,
  `foreground_style(Color)` (no `.color()`), `background(Color)`,
  `border(Color, width)`, `tint(Color)`, `frame(width/height/alignment)`,
  `opacity`, `hidden`, `corner_radius`, `line_limit`, `text_alignment`,
  `truncation_mode`, `offset`, `position`, `z_index`, `pointer_events`,
  `on_tap_gesture`.
- **Typography** (`Font` + `TextStyle`): `Font::large_title()`…`caption2()` emit
  the predefined `TEXT_STYLE` (renderer-owned size/weight); `Font::custom(name,
  size)`, `Font::system(size)`, `Font::system_weight(size, weight)`, and
  `Font::custom_full(name, size, weight, design)` emit the raw
  `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_DESIGN` axes. `FontFamily` is a
  `STRING` property via `Node::string_properties`.
- **`frame` infinity sugar**: infinite `width`/`height` hints (`f32::INFINITY`,
  SwiftUI `maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity`) normalize to the `size::FILL`
  sentinel on emission.
- **Composition**: blanket `ViewExt::modifier` + `ViewModifier` for custom
  modifiers; `Modified<V, M>` wrapper.
- **Alignment enum** (`Align`): Leading/Center/Trailing/Fill.
- **`Color` rules**: no `.color()` modifier; foreground is `.foreground_style(_:)`.
- **Design tokens**: `Color` is `Literal(u32)` | `Token(&'static str)` —
  `Color::token("color.primary")` (and `dark.*` paths) usable as a View and in
  every color-taking modifier (`foreground_style`, `background`, `border`,
  `tint`); token refs emit as the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type via
  `Node::token_properties` (spec/TOKENS.md).
- **`Theme` / `AdaptiveTheme` (global overrides)**: re-exports
  `pathland_engine::Theme` (single-value builders `color`/`f32`/`string`/… for
  one scheme) and `AdaptiveTheme { light, dark }`. Emit once at mount via
  `Engine::apply_theme` (light) / `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme` (light + the
  `dark.`-prefixed dark theme; STRING values arena-alloc'd).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **`SizeThatFits` (SIZE_THAT_FITS 0x17 / FIT_QUERY LIST / FIT_CHANGED)** is
  **authored** (`SizeThatFits::new(Vec<Fit>)` + `Fit::new(view, minWidth)` /
  `Fit::any`) emitting the slot + its single selected child + the `FIT_QUERY`
  list (the engine's LIST value-type emission); **reactive selection is fixed** —
  only the Java DSL's structural slot reacts to `FIT_CHANGED`.
- `TextField`'s `PROMPT` and `Color`/`Image` sources are stored as placeholder
  values only (STRING props are supported via `Node::string_properties`, but
  these builders don't set them yet).
- No `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` helpers, no `TOGGLE_STYLE`-typed API (raw u8).

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-view` — builder, modifier chaining, `assign_ids`,
tap-gesture listener wiring, new-component building.

content.text:
Research complete. The Rust DSL is `lib/rust/crates/pathland-view` (`no_std` + `alloc`), structural only — no signals, styles, or actions. Consumers of its builder surface: its own tests/doctests, `pathland-render-gtk-demo`, and tests in `pathland-render-gtk/host.rs` + `pathland-core-transport/batch.rs` (`pathland-view-native` only uses `Component`/`Node`).

Here's the plan and the open decisions.

# Plan: DSL v2 surface in the Rust DSL (`pathland-view`)

## Current shape
- Construction: `Text::new(&str)`, `VStack::new().children(vec![...])`, free fns (`text`, `spacer`, `button`, `icon`), macros (`vstack!`, `hstack!`).
- Modifiers: `ViewExt::with<M: ViewModifier>(self, m) -> Modified<Self, M>` single, **plus ~25 per-modifier sugar methods** (`.padding`, `.font_size`, `.foreground_style`, `.frame`, `.on_tap_gesture`, …).
- `Modified<V, M>` wrapper applies a modifier at `build()`.
- Only `FontDesignMod` carries a `Mod` suffix (merges with the `FontDesign` enum).
- No config type, no styles, no signals/actions.

## Target surface (Rust, §9.3 mapping)
```rust
// static or chained, any order
VStack::with(|v| v.spacing(8.0).alignment(Align::Center))
      .modifiers((Padding(16.0), Frame::w_h(100.0, 24.0)))
      .children([text("a"), text("b")]);          // or vstack![…]

text("hi").modifiers((FontSize(20.0), ForegroundStyle(Color::argb(…))));
```
Realization (per spec §9.3 "assoc fn + trait + macros"):
- **values** → inherent `Type::with(|c| …)` (static) + a `ViewExt::with` trait method (chained); config is mutable/fluent.
- **modifiers** → `Type::modifiers(…)` static + `ViewExt::modifiers` chained, returning a `Modified<V>` that applies the list at `build()`. `Modified<V>` also implements the other ops (delegating) so order is independent.
- **children** → `Type::children([…])` static + a `Children` trait method for content-bearing views; macros remain the ergonomic entry.
- **no `Mod` suffix**: rename `FontDesignMod` → `FontDesign` (the enum `impl ViewModifier`); delete the wrapper.

## Work items
1. **Ops plumbing**: `ViewExt` (`with`/`modifiers`), a `Children` trait, and `Modified<V>` (Vec of modifiers) with blanket delegating impls for order-independence. Validate that an inherent assoc fn `Type::with` coexists with a trait method `.with` (Rust allows it via method resolution; will confirm with a compile check early; fallback = macros for static entry).
2. **Config**: add a `Config` per view with fluent setters; `build()` reads it. (~30 small structs.)
3. **No-`Mod`**: `FontDesignMod` → `FontDesign`; grep for any other `*Mod` (only this one).
4. **Children coverage**: ensure `children(...)` on all content-bearing views (stacks, grids, scroll, lazy*, Picker/Menu, Button if in scope).
5. **Migrate**: demo `main.rs`; `host.rs`/`batch.rs` tests; the crate's tests + doctests.
6. **Docs/status**: update `pathland-view/status.md`; fix `spec/DSL.md` §5.6 + §10 Rust columns (still stale `.with(Card)` → `.modifiers(…)`).
7. **Verify**: `cargo test -p pathland-view`, workspace `cargo test`, and `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (no_std/wasm guard).

## Non-goals (unless you want them)
Signals, two-way bindings, actions, and styles (`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/…) do not exist in the Rust DSL; the "config shared with styles" half of the design is Java-only today.

## Open decisions
1. **Scope** — structural only (three ops + config + no-`Mod`), or also add the missing features (signals/actions/styles)?
2. **`modifiers(...)` ergonomics** — tuple `(A, B)` (no alloc, heterogeneous), `Vec<Box<dyn ViewModifier>>` (alloc, consistent with `children`), or a `modifiers![A, B]` macro?
3. **Per-modifier sugar** — drop `.padding()`/`.font_size()`/… in favor of `.modifiers(...)` (spec says no sugar on the view), or keep them as convenience alongside `.modifiers(...)`?

questions.question: How much of the design should the Rust implementation cover?

options.label: Structural only (Recommended)
options.description: Three operations + per-view config + no Mod suffix on the existing structural DSL. No signals/actions/styles (the Rust DSL has none).

options.label: Add styles too
options.description: Also add ButtonStyle/LabelStyle/… and make a control's makeBody receive the shared config. Larger, new feature area.

options.label: Full parity
options.description: Also add signals, two-way bindings, and actions to match the Java DSL. Very large.

questions.question: How should the Rust modifiers(...) list be expressed?

options.label: Tuple (A, B) (Recommended)
options.description: Heterogeneous, zero-alloc: .modifiers((Padding(16.0), FontSize(20.0))). Tuple trait with macro impls for arities.

options.label: Vec<Box<dyn ViewModifier>>
options.description: Heterogeneous with alloc, consistent with children(Vec<Box<dyn View>>); more verbose at call sites.

options.label: modifiers![A, B] macro
options.description: A macro that boxes the list; concise but a new macro to learn.

questions.question: Keep the existing per-modifier sugar methods (.padding/.font_size/...) alongside .modifiers(...)?

options.label: Drop them (Recommended)
options.description: Only .modifiers(...) (and the macros) per the spec's 'no sugar on the view type'. Cleanest, matches the contract.

options.label: Keep as convenience
options.description: Keep .padding(16.0) etc. as thin wrappers over .modifiers(...). Lower migration churn, but the surface diverges from the spec.

1: //! Diff-based reactive emitter.
2: //!
3: //! The engine holds the application's retained view tree and emits the
4: //! declarative structure as `TREE`/`PARAMETER` opcodes into the 16-byte ring
5: //! buffer (VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment). It does not
6: //! compute rects or layout; native renderers lay out their own elements.
7: //!
8: //! Emission is diff-based: on each `emit` the engine compares the current tree
9: //! against a snapshot of what it last emitted and writes only the opcodes for
10: //! nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits zero opcodes.
11: //!
12: //! The emit pass performs zero dynamic heap allocations in the steady state.
13: //!
14: //! ## Signals
15: //!
16: //! Nodes may bind their text or a property to a [`crate::SignalId`]. The engine
17: //! resolves those bindings during emit (recording the dependency) and re-emits
18: //! only the affected nodes on [`Engine::set_signal`] — no full tree walk.
19:

32: /// Encode a `LIST` property's arena entry: `[u32 count][f32 × count]`
33: /// (spec/OPCODE.md §Value types — a `FIT_QUERY` threshold table).
34: fn encode_list(values: &[f32]) -> Vec<u8> {
35:     let mut bytes = vec![0u8; 4 + 4 * values.len()];
36:     bytes[0..4].copy_from_slice(&(values.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
37:     for (i, value) in values.iter().enumerate() {
38:         let o = 4 + 4 * i;
39:         bytes[o..o + 4].copy_from_slice(&value.to_bits().to_le_bytes());
40:     }
41:     bytes
42: }

75: /// The diff-based reactive emitter.
76: ///
77: /// `Engine` keeps the snapshot of what was last emitted and owns the signal
78: /// store. Calling `emit` with a (possibly mutated) retained tree writes only
79: /// the delta opcodes; `set_signal` writes deltas for only the bound nodes.
80: pub struct Engine {
81:     /// nodeId to last emitted state (a preallocated slab; node ids are dense).
82:     snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,
83:     /// Monotonic generation stamp for the current pass.
84:     gen: u64,
85:     /// Reactive signal store (owns values + the reverse dependency index).
86:     store: SignalStore,
87: }

93: }

95: impl Engine {
96:     pub fn new() -> Self {
97:         Self {
98:             snapshot: Vec::new(),
99:             gen: 0,
100:             store: SignalStore::default(),
101:         }
102:     }
103: 
104:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
105:     pub fn emit(
106:         &mut self,
107:         root: &Node,
108:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
109:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_core::RingError> {
110:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
111:         // Rebuild the signal dependency index from scratch; reconcile re-adds
112:         // the bindings this tree actually uses, so stale subscriptions vanish.
113:         self.store.clear_deps();
114:         let mut out = 0usize;
115:         self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?;
116: 
117:         for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
118:             if let Some(s) = slot {
119:                 if s.gen != self.gen {
120:                     guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;
121:                     out += 1;
122:                     *slot = None;
123:                 }
124:             }
125:         }
126:         Ok(EmitResult { opcodes: out })
127:     }

129:     /// Number of nodes tracked in the snapshot (diagnostics).
130:     pub fn tracked_nodes(&self) -> usize {
131:         self.snapshot.iter().filter(|s| s.is_some()).count()
132:     }

136:     /// tokens; a `dark.`-prefixed path overrides the dark variant
137:     /// (spec/TOKENS.md). Returns the arena offset of the token path.
138:     pub fn set_design_token(
139:         &mut self,
140:         path: &str,
141:         value_type: u8,
142:         value: u32,
143:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
144:     ) -> Result<u32, pathland_core::RingError> {
145:         guest.set_design_token(path, value_type, value)
146:     }

148:     /// Emit a batch of global design-token overrides ([`Theme`](crate::Theme))
149:     /// as `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` opcodes. `STRING`-valued overrides allocate
150:     /// their value into the guest arena first (the wire carries an arena ref).
151:     ///
152:     /// Overrides are renderer-global: they never re-emit nodes and are not part
153:     /// of the diff. Emit once at mount, before the tree.
154:     pub fn apply_theme(
155:         &mut self,
156:         theme: &crate::Theme,
157:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
158:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
159:         for (path, value) in theme.iter() {
160:             self.emit_token_override(path, value, guest)?;
161:         }
162:         Ok(())
163:     }

165:     /// Emit an adaptive theme ([`AdaptiveTheme`](crate::AdaptiveTheme)): the
166:     /// **light** theme's overrides as base tokens, the **dark** theme's with the
167:     /// `dark.` scheme prefix (spec/TOKENS.md).
168:     pub fn apply_adaptive_theme(
169:         &mut self,
170:         adaptive: &crate::AdaptiveTheme,
171:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
172:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
173:         self.apply_theme(&adaptive.light, guest)?;
174:         for (path, value) in adaptive.dark.iter() {
175:             let dark_path = if path.starts_with("dark.") {
176:                 path.to_string()
177:             } else {
178:                 alloc::format!("dark.{path}")
179:             };
180:             self.emit_token_override(&dark_path, value, guest)?;
181:         }
182:         Ok(())
183:     }

185:     /// Emit one `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override, arena-allocating STRING values.
186:     fn emit_token_override(
187:         &mut self,
188:         path: &str,
189:         value: &pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue,
190:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
191:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
192:         use pathland_core::tokens::TokenValue;
193:         match value {
194:             TokenValue::Str(s) => {
195:                 let ref_ = guest
196:                     .alloc_str(s)
197:                     .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
198:                 guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), ref_)?;
199:             }
200:             _ => {
201:                 if let Some(bits) = value.to_bits() {
202:                     guest.set_design_token(path, value.value_type(), bits)?;
203:                 }
204:             }
205:         }
206:         Ok(())
207:     }

221:     /// Replace a signal's value and re-emit only the nodes that depend on it.
222:     ///
223:     /// Writes `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` deltas for the bound nodes whose
224:     /// materialized value changed. Returns the number of opcodes written.
225:     pub fn set_signal(
226:         &mut self,
227:         id: SignalId,
228:         value: SignalValue,
229:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
230:     ) -> Result<usize, pathland_core::RingError> {
231:         if !self.store.set(id, value) {
232:             return Ok(0);
233:         }
234:         let mut out = 0usize;
235:         let deps: Vec<Dep> = self.store.deps(id).to_vec();
236:         for dep in deps {
237:             match dep {
238:                 Dep::Text { node } => {
239:                     let new_text: Option<String> = self
240:                         .store
241:                         .get(id)
242:                         .and_then(SignalValue::to_text)
243:                         .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
244:                     let prev_text = self.snapshot_text(node);
245:                     if new_text.as_deref() != prev_text {
246:                         if let Some(t) = new_text.as_deref() {
247:                             guest.set_text(node, t)?;
248:                             out += 1;
249:                         }
250:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
251:                             s.text = new_text;
252:                         }
253:                     }
254:                 }
255:                 Dep::Property { node, prop } => {
256:                     let new_value = self
257:                         .store
258:                         .get(id)
259:                         .and_then(SignalValue::to_property_u32);
260:                     let prev_value = self.snapshot_property(node, prop);
261:                     if new_value != prev_value {
262:                         if let Some(v) = new_value {
263:                             guest.set_property(node, prop, value_type_for(prop), v)?;
264:                             out += 1;
265:                         }
266:                         if let Some(s) = self.snapshot_mut(node) {
267:                             match new_value {
268:                                 Some(v) => {
269:                                     s.properties.insert(prop, v);
270:                                 }
271:                                 None => {
272:                                     s.properties.remove(&prop);
273:                                 }
274:                             }
275:                         }
276:                     }
277:                 }
278:             }
279:         }
280:         Ok(out)
281:     }

303:     fn slot_mut(&mut self, id: u32) -> &mut Option<SnapshotNode> {
304:         let idx = id as usize;
305:         if self.snapshot.len() <= idx {
306:             self.snapshot.resize(idx + 1, None);
307:         }
308:         &mut self.snapshot[idx]

311:     #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
312:     fn reconcile_node(
313:         &mut self,
314:         node: &Node,
315:         parent: Option<u32>,
316:         index: usize,
317:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
318:         out: &mut usize,
319:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_core::RingError> {
320:         let component_type = component_type_id(&node.component);
321: 
322:         // Resolve bindings (owned) before taking the mutable snapshot borrow.
323:         let bound_text: Option<String> = node
324:             .text_binding
325:             .and_then(|sid| self.store.get(sid))
326:             .and_then(SignalValue::to_text)
327:             .map(ToOwned::to_owned);
328: 
329:         let merged_props: Option<BTreeMap<u16, u32>> = if node.property_bindings.is_empty() {
330:             None
331:         } else {
332:             let mut m = node.properties.clone();
333:             for (prop, sid) in &node.property_bindings {
334:                 if let Some(v) = self.store.get(*sid).and_then(SignalValue::to_property_u32) {
335:                     m.insert(*prop, v);
336:                 }
337:             }
338:             Some(m)
339:         };
340: 
341:         let text_borrowed: Option<&str> = match (&bound_text, &node.component) {
342:             (Some(s), _) => Some(s.as_str()),
343:             (None, Component::Text { text }) => Some(text.as_str()),
344:             (None, Component::Button { label }) => Some(label.as_str()),
345:             _ => None,
346:         };
347:         let props: &BTreeMap<u16, u32> = merged_props.as_ref().unwrap_or(&node.properties);
348:         let token_refs = &node.token_properties;
349:         let strings = &node.string_properties;
350:         let lists = &node.list_properties;
351: 
352:         let prev = self.slot_mut(node.id).take();
353:         let token_changed = match &prev {
354:             Some(p) => p.token_refs.len() != token_refs.len()
355:                 || p.token_refs
356:                     .iter()
357:                     .any(|(prop, (old, _))| token_refs.get(prop) != Some(old)),
358:             None => !token_refs.is_empty(),
359:         };
360:         let strings_changed = match &prev {
361:             Some(p) => {
362:                 p.string_properties.len() != strings.len()
363:                     || p.string_properties
364:                         .iter()
365:                         .any(|(prop, (old, _))| strings.get(prop) != Some(old))
366:             }
367:             None => !strings.is_empty(),
368:         };
369:         let lists_changed = match &prev {
370:             Some(p) => {
371:                 p.list_properties.len() != lists.len()
372:                     || p.list_properties
373:                         .iter()
374:                         .any(|(prop, (old, _))| lists.get(prop) != Some(old))
375:             }
376:             None => !lists.is_empty(),
377:         };
378:         let props_changed = match &prev {
379:             Some(p) => &p.properties != props || token_changed || strings_changed || lists_changed,
380:             None => !props.is_empty() || !token_refs.is_empty() || !strings.is_empty() || !lists.is_empty(),
381:         };
382:         let text_changed = match &prev {
383:             Some(p) => p.text.as_deref() != text_borrowed,
384:             None => text_borrowed.is_some(),
385:         };
386: 
387:         // Token-ref emission. Built only on mount or when a ref changed, so a
388:         // steady-state pass performs no heap allocations (the unchanged refs'
389:         // arena offsets are reused from the previous snapshot below).
390:         let mut token_emit: Option<BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>> = None;
391:         // String-property emission, built only on mount / when a value changed
392:         // (arena offsets reused from the previous snapshot otherwise).
393:         let mut string_emit: Option<BTreeMap<u16, (String, u32)>> = None;
394:         // List-property emission, built only on mount / when a value changed
395:         // (arena offsets reused from the previous snapshot otherwise).
396:         let mut list_emit: Option<BTreeMap<u16, (Vec<f32>, u32)>> = None;
397: 
398:         // Properties in two passes — literals (skipping token-ref'd ids) then
399:         // token refs — so the steady-state emit performs no heap allocations.
400:         match &prev {
401:             None => {
402:                 guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
403:                 *out += 1;
404:                 if let Some(p) = parent {
405:                     guest.insert_child(p, node.id, index as u32)?;
406:                     *out += 1;
407:                 }
408:                 for (prop, value) in props {
409:                     if token_refs.contains_key(prop) {
410:                         continue;
411:                     }
412:                     guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
413:                     *out += 1;
414:                 }
415:                 if !token_refs.is_empty() {
416:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
417:                     for (prop, path) in token_refs {
418:                         let arena = guest
419:                             .alloc_str(path)
420:                             .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
421:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN, arena)?;
422:                         *out += 1;
423:                         m.insert(*prop, (path.clone(), arena));
424:                     }
425:                     token_emit = Some(m);
426:                 }
427:                 if !strings.is_empty() {
428:                     let mut m = BTreeMap::new();
429:                     for (prop, value) in strings {
430:                         let arena = guest
431:                             .alloc_str(value)
432:                             .map_err(|_| pathland_core::RingError::Full)?;
433:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type::STRING, arena)?;
434:                         *out += 1;
435:                         m.insert(*prop, (value.clone(), arena));
436:                     }
437:                     string_emit = Some(m);
438:                 }
439:                 if !lists.is_empty() {

441:                     for (prop, values) in lists {
442:                         let bytes = encode_list(values);

444:                             .alloc(&bytes)

I dug into the engine/native layers. "Full parity" is much larger than the Rust DSL alone — the Rust core already has a signal store, but most of the Java DSL's higher layers have no Rust equivalent yet.

## What already exists in Rust
- **Signals (engine-level)**: `Engine::create_signal`/`get_signal`/`set_signal` with reverse-dependency partial re-emit (`pathland-engine/src/engine.rs:211`, `signal.rs`).
- **Node bindings**: `Node.text_binding`, `property_bindings` (`node.rs:42,45`) — but the DSL never sets them.
- **Gestures**: `Gesture::Tap` callback (`node.rs:92`), used by `on_tap_gesture` + `TapRecognizer`.
- **Theme/tokens**: `Engine::apply_theme`/`apply_adaptive_theme`, `Color::token`.

## What "full parity" is missing (Java features with no Rust equivalent)
1. **Signals API** — `signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`untracked`, equality, glitch-free flush (engine has only raw create/set/get; no computed/effect).
2. **DSL binding** — views/modifiers binding text/properties to signals (needs a build-time signal registry; today `View::build(&self) -> Node` has no engine/context).
3. **Two-way bindings** — value/text/date **input sinks** + routing (`Node` has no `valueInput`/`textInput`; the Java `RenderResult` registries don't exist).
4. **Actions** — `Button` action (`Component::Button` is a leaf label; only tap gestures exist).
5. **Styles + environment** — `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`AudioStyle`/`VideoStyle`, `EnvironmentKey` scoping, Composite Override Mode (all absent).
6. **Navigation** — `Router`/`RouteTable`/`NavigationContainer`/`NavigationLink` (absent; the demo notes "no Rust router yet").
7. **Conditional/structural slots** — `Conditional.when` (absent; Rust rebuilds the tree by hand).
8. **Persisted state** — `State<T>`/`StateStore`/`PersistentState` (absent; Java has in-memory + Redis).
9. **SizeThatFits** — selection is fixed (no `FIT_CHANGED` reaction).

This spans **four crates** (`pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-view-native`) under `no_std`/wasm constraints. It's a multi-milestone effort, not one pass.

## Proposed roadmap
- **Phase 0 — authoring surface (self-contained):** the three operations (`with`/`modifiers`/`children`, static+chained, any order), per-view `Config`, tuple `modifiers(...)`, drop the ~25 sugar methods, `FontDesignMod → FontDesign`, migrate demo/`host.rs`/`batch.rs`/tests, update `status.md` + fix `spec/DSL.md` §5.6/§10 Rust columns. *No engine change.*
- **Phase 1 — signals + binding:** engine computed/effects (or DSL wrappers), a build-time signal registry (`View::build(ctx)` or `SignalId` config), `Text`/property binding.
- **Phase 2 — two-way + actions:** input sinks + routing, `Button`/`Toggle`/`Slider`/`TextField` controls, render-gtk event plumbing.
- **Phase 3 — styles + environment:** scoping + `*Style` + Composite Override Mode.
- **Phase 4 — navigation + conditional:** `Router`/`RouteTable`/`NavigationContainer`/`NavigationLink`/`Conditional`.
- **Phase 5 — persisted state:** `StateStore` trait + in-memory (+ optional desktop backends).

Phase 0 fully delivers the design you asked for on the *structural* DSL; Phases 1–5 are additive and independently reviewable.

Given the size, I'd implement **Phase 0 first** and land it, then proceed phase by phase. One question:

Understood — full parity, delivered phase by phase with a checkpoint after each. Here is the complete plan.

# Plan: Rust DSL full parity with the DSL v2 design

## Guiding constraints
- **No wire change**: same opcodes/bytes for an equivalent tree.
- **`no_std` + `alloc`**, must keep compiling for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (`lib/rust/check-wasm.sh`).
- **Checkpoint per phase**: each phase compiles, tests green, `status.md` updated, review before the next.
- **Spec consistency**: fix stale Rust columns in `spec/DSL.md` as the surface lands.

## Phase 0 — authoring surface (structural DSL, no engine change)
**Goal:** the three operations + config + no-`Mod` + tuple modifiers, on the existing structural DSL.
- **Ops plumbing** in `pathland-view/src/lib.rs`:
  - `ModifierList` trait (macro impls for tuples `(A,)`, `(A,B)`, …) → `Vec<Box<dyn ViewModifier>>`.
  - `ViewExt::modifiers<L: ModifierList>(self, list) -> Modified<Self>`; `Modified<V>` wraps a view + modifier list, applies at `build()`.
  - `Configurable` trait (`type Config; fn config_mut(&mut self) -> &mut Self::Config`) + `ViewExt::with(self, f)` for chaining.
  - `Children` trait for content-bearing views; `ViewExt::children(self, Vec<Box<dyn View>>) -> Self`.
  - **Static entries** `Type::with(|c| …)`, `Type::modifiers((…))`, `Type::children([…])` as inherent assoc fns; trait methods cover chaining. *Validate inherent-assoc + trait-method coexistence with a compile check first; fallback = macros for the static entry.*
  - `Modified<V>` implements `Configurable`/`Children` (delegating) so order is fully independent.
  - **Config structs** per view with fluent `&mut self` setters (`VStackConfig::spacing/alignment`, …).
- **Drop** the ~25 `ViewExt` sugar methods (`.padding`, `.font_size`, `.foreground_style`, `.frame`, `.pointer_events`, `.on_tap_gesture`, …) → `.modifiers((Padding(16.0), …))`; expose `TapGesture::new(f)` for gestures.
- **No `Mod`**: `FontDesignMod` → `FontDesign` (the enum `impl ViewModifier`); delete the wrapper.
- **Surface gaps** (cheap, include): named shapes (`Rectangle`/`Circle`/`Capsule`/`Ellipse`/`RoundedRectangle`), `GridRow`, and fill in `Config` for every control so `with(...)` is real (not just stacks).
- **Migrate**: `pathland-render-gtk-demo/main.rs`, `pathland-render-gtk/src/host.rs` tests, `pathland-core-transport/src/batch.rs` tests, crate tests + doctests.
- **Docs**: `pathland-view/status.md`; fix `spec/DSL.md` §5.6/§10 Rust columns and §4.4 gesture row.
- **Verify**: `cargo test -p pathland-view`, workspace `cargo test`, `check-wasm.sh`.

## Phase 1 — signals + binding
- **Engine**: add computed signals + effects with equality suppression, synchronous/glitch-free flush (extend `SignalStore`), or a DSL-level reactive layer over `SignalId`.
- **Build context**: give the DSL a signal registry. Decision to confirm at checkpoint: `View::build(&self, ctx: &mut BuildContext)` (faithful, breaks custom views) **vs** `SignalId`-in-config (no trait change).
- **DSL**: `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` (or `SignalId` handles); `Text::with(|t| t.text(signal))` and property bindings (`ForegroundStyle`/`FontSize`/… accepting signals) setting `Node.text_binding`/`property_bindings`.
- **Verify**: partial-emit tests (bind → set → only bound node re-emits; unchanged → zero opcodes).

## Phase 2 — two-way bindings + actions
- **Engine/app**: input sinks for value/text/date + routing (Java's `RenderResult` equivalent), wired in `render-gtk` + the demo event loop.
- **DSL**: `Button` action; `Toggle`/`Slider`/`Stepper`/`TextField`/`TextEditor`/`DatePicker`/`Picker`/`Menu`/`ColorPicker` value bindings + `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID`/`EVENT_LISTENERS`; `TextField`'s `PROMPT` and `Image` source via `string_properties`.
- **Verify**: round-trip tests (`TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED`/`DATE_CHANGED` write the bound signal → delta re-emitted).

## Phase 3 — styles + environment
- **Environment**: subtree scoping of typed keys (Rust `no_std` has no thread-local — decision at checkpoint: `BuildContext` scope stack vs `Cell`-based ambient scope).
- **Styles**: `Style`/`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`AudioStyle`/`VideoStyle` as `ViewModifier`s reading a shared `Config`; `PlainButtonStyle`/`BorderedButtonStyle`, `DefaultLabelStyle`/`TitleOnly`/`IconOnly`, `NativeAudio/VideoStyle`; Button content precedence (child > title > style).
- **Renderer**: Composite Override Mode wiring in `render-gtk`.

## Phase 4 — navigation + conditional
- `Conditional.when` structural slot (reconcile → `TREE` deltas), `Router`/`RouteTable`/`Params`/`Route`, `NavigationContainer` (`ROUTE`/`NAV_DEPTH`/`NAV_CHROME`/`TRANSITION`), `NavigationLink`, `NavigationIntent`, `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH`; `NAVIGATE` handling in the demo/renderer.

## Phase 5 — persisted state
- `StateStore` trait + `PersistentState` + `State<T>`, an in-memory `StateStore` (no_std) and optional desktop/browser backends; wire `State` fields (Rust has no annotation processor — explicit/explicit-registration wiring).

## Cross-cutting per phase
- `status.md` updated (mandatory), spec conformance cross-checks, golden-vector/byte parity where relevant, `no_std`/wasm guard, and demo migrated so it stays the living example.

## Risks / decisions flagged for checkpoints
- Inherent-assoc-fn vs trait-method name coexistence (validated in Phase 0).
- `View::build` signature change vs `SignalId`-in-config (Phase 1).
- Ambient environment scoping without thread-locals (Phase 3).
- Input-routing ownership (engine `Node` vs app-side registries) (Phase 2).

I'll start with **Phase 0** and stop for review before Phase 1. Ready to begin on approval.

# pathland-view (Rust DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 9, 2026

The SwiftUI-style **view DSL** (`no_std`) building `pathland_engine::Node`
trees. Protocol contract: `spec/`, authoring surface: `spec/DSL.md`.

## Implemented

- **The three authoring operations** (spec/DSL.md §2): every concrete view
  exposes **values** (`Type::with(|c| …)` static / `view.with(|c| …)` chained),
  **modifiers** (`Type::modifiers((A, B))` / `view.modifiers((A, B))`, single or
  tuple list) and, for content-bearing views, **children**
  (`Type::children(vec![…])` / `view.children(vec![…])`). The three may be used
  at creation or chained, in any order.
- **Per-view `Config`** (`TextConfig`, `StackConfig`, `GridConfig`,
  `RangeConfig`, …) with fluent setters, consumed by the value builders. Values
  move structural properties (`spacing`/`alignment`/grid counts) into the config
  (no longer modifiers).
- **Views**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `ScrollView`, `LazyVGrid`,
  `LazyHGrid`, `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `Text`, `Button`, `Spacer`,
  `Icon` (semantic symbols via `IconName` + `icon(…)`), `Image` (sets
  `IMAGE_SOURCE`), `Color` (dual identity: a layout-greedy View *and* a value
  passed into style modifiers), `Shape` + named `Rectangle`/`Circle`/`Capsule`/
  `Ellipse`, `Divider`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Toggle`, `Slider`,
  `TextField` (sets `PROMPT`), `TextEditor`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`,
  `Menu`, `ColorPicker` (+ the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros and
  `text`/`spacer`/`button`/`icon`/`image` free functions).
- **Modifiers** (decoupled values applied via `modifiers(...)`): `Padding`,
  `FontSize`, `FontWeight`, `Font(Font)`, `FontFamily`, `FontDesign` (the enum
  *is* the modifier), `ForegroundStyle` (no `.color()`), `Background`, `Border`,
  `Tint`, `Frame`, `Opacity`, `Hidden`, `CornerRadius`, `LineLimit`,
  `TextAlignment`, `TruncationMode`, `Offset`, `Position`, `ZIndex`,
  `PointerEvents`, `TapGesture` (`TapGesture::new(f)`).
- **No `Mod` suffix**: modifiers are named for the modifier they apply;
  `FontDesignMod` is gone (`FontDesign` is the modifier).
- **Typography** (`Font` + `TextStyle`): `Font::large_title()`…`caption2()` emit
  the predefined `TEXT_STYLE` (renderer-owned size/weight); `Font::custom(name,
  size)`, `Font::system(size)`, `Font::system_weight(size, weight)`, and
  `Font::custom_full(name, size, weight, design)` emit the raw
  `FONT_FAMILY`/`FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT`/`FONT_DESIGN` axes.
- **`Frame` infinity**: infinite `width`/`height` hints (`f32::INFINITY`,
  SwiftUI `maxWidth/maxHeight: .infinity`) normalize to the `size::FILL`
  sentinel on emission.
- **Composition**: blanket `ViewExt::modifiers` + `ViewModifier` for custom
  modifiers; `Modified<V>` wrapper (applies its modifier list at `build`).
  `Modified<V>` implements `Configurable`/`Children` (delegating) so the three
  operations are order-independent.
- **Alignment enum** (`Align`): Leading/Center/Trailing.
- **Design tokens**: `Color` is `Literal(u32)` | `Token(&'static str)` —
  `Color::token("color.primary")` (and `dark.*` paths) usable as a View and in
  every color-taking modifier; token refs emit as the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type
  via `Node::token_properties` (spec/TOKENS.md).
- **`Theme` / `AdaptiveTheme` (global overrides)**: re-exports
  `pathland_engine::Theme` and `AdaptiveTheme { light, dark }`. Emit once at
  mount via `Engine::apply_theme` / `Engine::apply_adaptive_theme`.

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Signals / two-way bindings / actions / styles / environment** — the Rust
  DSL is **structural only**. The engine already has a signal store
  (`Engine::create_signal`/`set_signal`, partial re-emit) and `Node` binding
  fields, but the DSL does not expose signals, control value bindings, `Button`
  actions, or `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/… Full Java-DSL parity is tracked as a
  phased effort (`spec/DSL.md` §9; `Button` carries a string label only).

content.text:
**Phase 0 checkpoint** — committed `11860ce1`.

## What landed
- **Three operations on every view** (order-independent, static or chained):
  - values: `Text::with(|c| { c.text("hi"); })` / `view.with(|c| …)`
  - modifiers: `.modifiers(Padding(16.0))` or `.modifiers((Padding(16.0), FontSize(12.0)))`
  - children: `VStack::children(vec![…])` / `.children(vec![…])` + `vstack!`/`hstack!`
- **Per-view `Config`** (`TextConfig`, `StackConfig`, `GridConfig`, `RangeConfig`, …) with fluent setters; structural values (spacing/alignment/grid counts) moved out of modifiers into the config.
- **No `Mod` suffix**: `FontDesignMod → FontDesign` (the enum *is* the modifier).
- New `ModifierList` (single/tuple, up to 12), `Configurable`, `Children`, `Modified<V>` (delegates the ops for order independence); named `Rectangle`/`Circle`/`Capsule`/`Ellipse`; `Image`/`TextField` now set their STRING properties.
- Migrated the GTK demo + `render-gtk`/`core-transport` tests; updated `status.md` and the stale Rust columns in `spec/DSL.md`.
- **No wire change**; stays `no_std`.

## Verification
- `cargo test --workspace` — all green (pathland-view: 40 unit + 3 doctests).
- `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` — OK.
- `cargo clippy -p pathland-view` — clean.

## Note
I ran `cargo fmt` which reformatted 48 files (the repo isn't rustfmt-clean); I reverted all unrelated churn and kept only the 6 intended files. Going forward I won't run workspace `cargo fmt`.

## Next — Phase 1 (signals + binding)
Engine computed/effects + a build-time signal registry, then DSL `Text`/property binding. It requires a design decision I flagged: change `View::build(&self) -> Node` to a context-carrying build **vs** `SignalId`-in-config. I'll bring a concrete recommendation when you give the go for Phase 1.

Proceed to Phase 1?

**Phase 1a checkpoint** — committed `89c63e10`.

## Landed
- **`pathland-engine`**: `SignalValueKind` trait; typed `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>` handles (Copy newtypes over `SignalId`); `IntoSignalId`; `Engine::signal` / `read` / `set`.
- **`pathland-view`**: re-exports; `Text::with(|t| { t.text_signal(sig); })` binds text; a `Bound` modifier + `FontSize/FontWeight/ForegroundStyle/Background/Opacity::bound(sig)` binds a property. A change re-emits **only** the bound node's `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`; unchanged emits zero.
- Tests (engine + view); `status.md` and the spec status-delta updated.

## Verified
`cargo test --workspace` green; `check-wasm.sh` OK; no new clippy warnings.

## Phase 1b — computed / effects: need a decision
This is the architectural fork. Java's `computed(|| count.get())` relies on an ambient reactive context (a thread-local). **`pathland-engine`/`pathland-view` are `#![no_std]`** (the wasm guard depends on it), so there is no thread-local. To keep Java-parity ambient reads I'd need:

- `Engine`'s store shared as `Rc<RefCell<SignalStore>>` (single-threaded, `RefCell` in `core` — no_std OK), so signal handles can `get()` without the engine.
- A computation stack + untracked flag in the store; `computed(f)` stores `Rc<dyn Fn() -> SignalValue>`; evaluation clones the closure out, drops the borrow, then calls it (avoids `RefCell` re-borrow panics). `set` marks transitive computeds dirty, recomputes in order, runs effects, and returns the changed cells so the engine re-emits their node deps.
- Handles stop being `Copy` (they hold the shared store) — a change from 1a.

This touches the engine's core (the emit hot path) and is the biggest single piece left in Phase 1.

- **Reactive signals (Phase 1)**: a shared `Runtime`
  (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local) with typed handles
  (`Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>`, `SignalValueKind`/`IntoSignalId`), value
  signals, **computed** (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained) and
  **effect** (runs immediately, then on dependency change) signals, and
  `untracked` reads; `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`. The DSL
  binds a node's **text** (`Text::with(|t| { t.text_signal(sig); })`) and a
  **property** (`FontSize::bound(sig)`, `FontWeight::bound`,
  `ForegroundStyle::bound`, `Background::bound`, `Opacity::bound`, or generic
  `Bound::new(prop, sig)`) to a signal, so a change re-emits only that node's
  `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` (a computed's change re-emits its bound nodes too).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **Two-way bindings (value controls) + actions**: no `valueInput`/`textInput`
  sinks or event routing; `Button` carries a string label only.
- **Styles / environment**: no `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/… or `EnvironmentKey`
  subtree scoping (Phase 3).
- **Navigation / conditional**: `Router`/`RouteTable`/`NavigationContainer`/
  `NavigationLink`/`Conditional` are absent (Phase 4); `Label`/`GridRow` are
  absent.
- **`SizeThatFits` (SIZE_THAT_FITS 0x17 / FIT_QUERY LIST / FIT_CHANGED)** is
  **authored** (`SizeThatFits::new(Vec<Fit>)` + `Fit::new(view, minWidth)` /
  `Fit::any`) emitting the slot + its single selected child + the `FIT_QUERY`
  list; **reactive selection is fixed** — only the Java DSL's structural slot
  reacts to `FIT_CHANGED`.
- No `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` helpers; `Toggle`/`Picker`/`Menu` lack typed
  value APIs (raw tokens only).

content.text:
**Phase 1 checkpoint** — committed `5299c2b2` (on top of `89c63e10`).

## Landed
- **`pathland-engine`**: replaced `SignalStore` with a shared **`Runtime`** (`Rc<RefCell<Store>>`, `no_std` — no thread-local; current computation is an explicit stack). Supports:
  - value signals, **computed** (lazy, memoized, equality-suppressed, chained), **effects** (immediate + on dep change), `untracked`;
  - typed handles `Signal<T>`/`WritableSignal<T>`; `Engine::signal`/`computed`/`effect`/`read`/`set`;
  - `set_signal` re-emits every changed cell's node deps, so a computed's bound nodes re-emit too.
- **`pathland-view`**: text/property binding (from 1a) + computed/effects available; tests for all.
- **GTK demo**: counter label is a **computed** over a count signal, tree built once; a tap writes the signal → engine re-emits **only** the bound label node.
- `pathland-view-native` + `status.md` (engine + view) updated.

## Verified
`cargo test --workspace` green (engine computed/effect/untracked + integration tests); `check-wasm.sh` OK; no new clippy warnings.

## Next — Phase 2: two-way bindings + actions
This adds **input sinks + event routing**: controls (`TextField`/`Toggle`/`Slider`/`Stepper`/`TextEditor`/`DatePicker`/`Picker`/`Menu`/`ColorPicker`) bind a writable signal and record a sink, the engine exposes a routing registry (tap/text/value/date), and the host forwards `EVENT` batches into the bound signals; plus a `Button` action. It touches `Node` (sink fields), the engine's `emit`/registries, `pathland-render-gtk` event plumbing, and the demo. It also needs one decision I'll flag: where the input registry lives (engine-exposed `RenderResult`-style vs app-side node sinks).

Shall I proceed to Phase 2?
go
Phase 2: two-way bindings + actions. Let me research the event/listener surface and how the renderer reports inputs.
