218: 
219: Pathland state is **Angular-style signals**. This is the non-negotiable
220: reactive core every DSL exposes.
221: 
222: ### 3.1 Signal surface
223: 
224: | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view.signal`) | Semantics |
225: |-----------|--------------------------------------|-----------|
226: | `signal(initial)` | `Signals.signal(T)` | a writable signal |
227: | `signal(name, initial)` | `Signals.signal(String, T)` | named (names surface in dependency errors) |
228: | `signal(initial, equal)` | `Signals.signal(T, BiPredicate<T,T>)` | custom equality |
229: | `computed(fn)` | `Signals.computed(Supplier<T>)` | lazy, memoized derived signal |
230: | `effect(fn)` | `Signals.effect(Runnable)` | runs immediately, then on dependency change |
231: | `untracked(fn)` | `Signals.untracked(Supplier<T>)` | reads without recording dependencies |
232: | `read()` | `get()` | current value |
233: | `write(v)` | `set(T)` | replace (no-op when equal) |
234: | `update(fn)` | `update(UnaryOperator<T>)` | derive from current and write |
235: | `asReadonly()` | `asReadonly()` | read-only view of a writable signal |

238: synchronous flush at the end of the outermost write, glitch-free propagation
239: (each computed recomputes at most once per flush), error caching, write
240: discipline, and circular-dependency detection.

243: reactive value — never a raw field *plus* a signal field for the same value. A
244: static value is authored through a raw config setter, which wraps a
245: `constant(...)` signal; the emitter treats a constant as a plain, non-reactive
246: property (no binding/effect). `WritableSignal<T>` extends `Signal<T>`, so a
247: two-way binding also satisfies a one-way member.

252: `TextField.with(t -> t.placeholder("…").text(writable))`,

257:    retained node) for the signal, and the emitter exposes routing registries to

259: 2. The host receives the control's raw event (`TEXT_CHANGED`,
260:    `VALUE_CHANGED`, `DATE_CHANGED`, or a composed tap) and calls the sink,
261:    which **writes into the signal**.
262: 3. The signal flush re-emits **only that node's** delta (`SET_TEXT`,
263:    `SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_DATE`) back through the emitter.

**Control guarantees** (from PRIMITIVES.md): a control without children renders
in **Native Token Mode** (native OS control); a control with a child subtree
renders in **Composite Override Mode** (custom chrome wrapped with native
gesture semantics). A **style** supplies that child subtree — the control owns
the native component + interaction, the style owns the content

value/text/date events by `BINDING_ID`, `ACTION_ID`, or the `EVENT_LISTENERS`

| Gesture | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) | Java DSL | Rust DSL |

then `POINTER_UP` on the same target (`EVENT_LISTENERS` bits 0|2). The
`TapGesture` modifier value declares those listeners and records the action;
the host routes the recognized tap via the emitter's tap-action registry.

Navigation is **structural reactivity over a route signal**
([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)): a
`NavigationContainer` is a structural container whose content function is
route-table matching. The wire surface is minimal and entirely optional:
`ROUTE` (MODIFIERS.md `0x2019`, a STRING current-path property on the slot),

slot), `NAV_CHROME` (MODIFIERS.md `0x201B`, an F32-enum chrome-mode property

the `NAVIGATE` event (EVENTS.md `0x0E`, host→guest). Renderers stay
stateless: they render whatever destination subtree the app emits and **may**
animate a swap when the `TRANSITION` hint is present, but must render normally
when they ignore it.

adds none. The container's chrome mode decides who supplies the navigation UI:

## The v2 surface (read the actual class files to confirm signatures)
Each concrete view exposes static entry points returning a `ViewBuilder`:
- `Text.with(t -> t.text("hello"))`  — value config
- `VStack.with(v -> v.alignment(HorizontalAlignment.LEADING).spacing(8)).children(a, b, c)` — configure + children
- `.modifiers(mod1, mod2, ...)` — apply modifier values (innermost-first), chainable in ANY order with `with(...)` and `children(...)`.

Every modifier class has a `with(Consumer<Config>)` static factory; single-value enum/Font/Style types are themselves the modifier.
`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.system(18f)`, `Font.headline()`, `TextAlignment.CENTER`, `Truncation.TAIL`, `TextCase.UPPERCASE`, `ControlSize.REGULAR`, `FontDesign.ROUNDED`, `FontStyle.ITALIC`, `PlainButtonStyle.INSTANCE` and other `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`AudioStyle`/`VideoStyle` instances are modifier VALUES you pass directly to `.modifiers(...)` — never a `*Mod.of(...)` wrapper.

13:   a structural slot (`SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17) emitting `FIT_QUERY` (LIST, ascending
14:   thresholds) + the single selected child — unselected candidates never transmit.
15:   The host routes `FIT_CHANGED` into the slot's fit sink
16:   (`RenderResult.fitInputs`, via `InputDispatcher`), which swaps the child through
17:   the structural reconcile (an unchanged index re-emits zero opcodes). The LIST
18:   value type is written by `FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`
19:   (`[count][f32 × count]` arena entries). A slot's selection is **retained node
20:   state** (`PathlandNode.fitSelection`): a parent-subtree re-render (an outer
21:   slot's candidate swap, a custom style body re-run) may rebuild a nested slot
22:   with a default index, so the reconcile **carries the previous selection across
23:   the match** (`Emitter.restoreFitSelection`) — a nested fit (the player bar's
24:   controls slot under the root row) keeps its candidate instead of resetting to
25:   compact (a reset would strand the DOM client, which never re-reports an
26:   unchanged width).

Both are fine — the files don't contain duplicate returns; your paste showed old vs. new side by side. Here's the actual reasoning behind the change.

## Why it changed

`content.environment(Environment.VIDEO_STYLE, this)` was a **`View` sugar method**:

```java
default <T> View environment(EnvironmentKey<T> key, T value) {
    return with(EnvironmentBinding.with(e -> e.key(key).value(value)));
}
```

Part of the cut (Phase 3, spec §5.6 "no per-modifier sugar on the `View` type") removed `font`/`navigate`/`push`/`replace`/`environment`/`onPathChange` from the `View` interface. That broke the four style interfaces (`ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`, `AudioStyle`, `VideoStyle`), whose `default View body(View content)` relied on `content.environment(...)`.

The replacement constructs the **same wrapper the sugar eventually created**, just without the middleman:

- `content.environment(key, value)` → `with(EnvironmentBinding.with(...))` → `EnvironmentBinding.body()` → `new EnvironmentView(content, key, value)`
- Now: directly `new EnvironmentView(content, key, value)` — skip the `EnvironmentBinding` object entirely (slightly cheaper, identical semantics).

`EnvironmentBinding.java:61` does exactly this internally — `return new EnvironmentView(content, (EnvironmentKey<Object>) key, value);` — so the change is consistent with the existing implementation.

**The ugly cast**: `EnvironmentView`'s constructor takes `EnvironmentKey<Object>` (raw-style field, matching what `EnvironmentValues.with(key, value)` wants), while the styles hold typed keys like `EnvironmentKey<VideoStyle>`. The double cast `(EnvironmentKey<Object>) (EnvironmentKey<?>)` is just generic variance workaround — same cast `EnvironmentBinding` does under `@SuppressWarnings`.

## Optional cleanup (if you want)

The cast is currently duplicated in 4 files. Two cleaner alternatives:

1. **Static typed factory on `EnvironmentView`** (hides the cast once):
   ```java
   @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
   static <T> EnvironmentView of(View content, EnvironmentKey<T> key, T value) {
       return new EnvironmentView(content, (EnvironmentKey<Object>) key, value);
   }
   ```
   Styles become `return EnvironmentView.of(content, Environment.VIDEO_STYLE, this);` — typed, no double cast.

2. **Widen `EnvironmentView` to `EnvironmentKey<?>`** and push the single unchecked cast into `render()` (same total casts, but the field is honest about wildcards).

Both are purely cosmetic — the behavior is identical today and all 482 tests pass. Want me to apply option 1 (or 2) in the next change, or leave the styles as they are?

**Title:** `Demo views: canonical chain order — modifiers → with → children (single modifiers call), nicely indented`

> **Convention for `lib/java/pathland-demo-views`** (and the demo tests) when authoring a view chain.

> The spec (DSL.md §2) allows the three operations in any order and their order does not affect emitted bytes; this issue standardizes **how the demos write them** so the code reads consistently:

> 3. **`.children(...)` last** — only for content-bearing views, as needed.
>
> `View.with(ViewModifier...)` (the plain-view chain) should not be used where the builder surface applies; modifiers belong in the single `.modifiers(...)`.

> **Indentation:** one chain operation per line; the vararg children each on their own line; `.modifiers(...)` arguments wrapped so every modifier sits on its own line.

> - Several files chain `.with(...)... .modifiers(...)` after `.children(...)`.
>
> **Scope:** rewrite the demo views to the canonical order + single-modifiers-call + per-line indentation. Behavior must stay byte-identical (spec conformance — a source-surface change only); verified by the existing demo/emitter tests.

1: package com.pathland.demo.music;
2: 
3: import com.pathland.view.*;
4: import com.pathland.view.signal.WritableSignal;
5: 
6: import static com.pathland.view.signal.Signals.computed;
7: 
8: /**
9:  * The bottom player bar: an app-driven {@link Audio} node whose custom
10:  * {@link PlayerControlsStyle} renders the whole bar surface — a centered row of
11:  * {@code [⏮] [play-pause] [⏭] | [cover art] [track title] | [volume]} over a
12:  * slim seek bar. The audio element is hidden; the controls drive it through the
13:  * bound media state, and playback events (time/ended/volume) flow back into the
14:  * same state.
15:  */
16: public final class PlayerBar implements View {
17: 
18:     private final WritableSignal<Integer> trackIndex;
19:     private final WritableSignal<Float> position;
20:     private final WritableSignal<Boolean> playing;
21:     private final WritableSignal<Float> volume;
22:     private final WritableSignal<Float> seekRequest;
23:     private final WritableSignal<Float> volumeRequest;
24: 
25:     /**
26:      * @param trackIndex    the current track index (drives the source + now-playing content)
27:      * @param position      the play position (seconds) — the seek-bar DISPLAY
28:      * @param playing       toggled by the play/pause button
29:      * @param volume        the volume slider's DISPLAY (0..1)
30:      * @param seekRequest   the SEEK command bound to {@code MEDIA_POSITION} (user drags only)
31:      * @param volumeRequest the VOLUME command bound to {@code MEDIA_VOLUME} (user drags only)
32:      */
33:     public PlayerBar(WritableSignal<Integer> trackIndex, WritableSignal<Float> position,
34:                      WritableSignal<Boolean> playing, WritableSignal<Float> volume,
35:                      WritableSignal<Float> seekRequest, WritableSignal<Float> volumeRequest) {
36:         this.trackIndex = trackIndex;
37:         this.position = position;
38:         this.playing = playing;
39:         this.volume = volume;
40:         this.seekRequest = seekRequest;
41:         this.volumeRequest = volumeRequest;
42:     }
43: 
44:     @Override
45:     public View body() {
46:         var current = computed(() -> MusicPlayerView.at(trackIndex.get()));
47:         // The whole bar surface is the audio node's custom style: a hidden media
48:         // element + the centered control row + the slim seek bar (app-driven).
49:         // The position/volume REPORTS flow to the DISPLAY signals (onPositionReport/
50:         // onVolumeReport); MEDIA_POSITION/MEDIA_VOLUME are bound to the seek/volume
51:         // COMMANDS, so a report never echoes back as a command (spec/EVENTS.md Media).
52:         return Audio.with(a -> a
53:                 .source(computed(() -> current.get().audio()))
54:                 .playing(playing)
55:                 .position(seekRequest)
56:                 .onPositionReport(position)
57:                 .volume(volumeRequest)
58:                 .onVolumeReport(volume)
59:                 .onEnded(this::ended))
60:                 .modifiers(PlayerControlsStyle.of(trackIndex, position, seekRequest, volume, volumeRequest))
61:                 .modifiers(Background.with(b -> b.color(MusicPlayerView.BAR_BG)))
62:                 .modifiers(Frame.with(f -> f.width(Commands.Size.FILL).height(MusicPlayerView.BAR_HEIGHT)));
63:     }
64: 
65:     /** The media ended: advance to the next track and restart from the top. The
66:      *  playing state is unchanged — the DOM client resumes playback when the new
67:      *  source lands. */
68:     private void ended() {
69:         trackIndex.update(i -> (i + 1) % MusicPlayerView.TRACKS.size());
70:         position.set(0f);
71:         seekRequest.set(0f);
72:     }
73: }

Committed as `00e99b45`. 

## Summary

Implemented issue #140 on branch `style/demo-chain-order`: reformed every demo-view chain in `pathland-demo-views` to the canonical order — **`.modifiers(...)`** (single call, all modifiers innermost-first, each on its own line) → **`.with(...)`** → **`.children(...)`**, one chain op per line with wrapped args. Leaves keep `.with(...)` + one `.modifiers(...)`; plain composites (PlayerBar, `SizeThatFits` results) stack modifiers in a single `.with(...)` (the builder surface doesn't apply there).

**27 files** reformatted (all demo views; the one test chain `new SplitNavDemo().with(...)` was already on a plain composite and left as-is).

**Verification:** demo-views 31 tests green; full Java reactor **482 tests green** — behavior unchanged, confirmed across the emitter/renderer suites (source-surface only per DSL.md §2).

**Note:** I used the two-statement form (`View content = VStack…; return new SectionCard(…, content);`) for the kitchen-sink sections that wrap in `SectionCard` — it avoids deep paren-pileups while keeping the chain itself in canonical order. Say the word if you'd rather keep those strictly inline.
PlayerBar should use the pattern with a configurator for inserting vaues into it. Can I somehow prevent developers from using the constrcutor when creating custom views?

Good question — this is about making custom views (like `PlayerBar`) follow the same `with(Consumer<Config>)` configurator pattern as the library views, and whether the public constructor can be suppressed. Let me investigate how the mechanism works today.

content.text:
I now have the complete picture. Here's the explanation of how `PersistedProcessor` works plus the refined plan (answers: 1=all five, 3=yes).

## How `PersistedProcessor` works

A JSR-269 **annotation processor** in `pathland-view-processor`, wired via `annotationProcessorPaths` — currently **only** in `pathland-demo-views/pom.xml` (library views and other modules don't run it).

Per compilation round (`@SupportedAnnotationTypes("*"` → runs always), `process()`:

1. Looks up `com.pathland.view.View` and `com.pathland.view.state.State` on the classpath; bails if absent.
2. Iterates the round's **root classes**; keeps only classes assignable to `View` (`types.isAssignable(erasure(type), viewErasure)`).
3. Scans each such class's **enclosed elements** for `FIELD` whose erasure is assignable to `State`, collecting field names (`persisted`).
4. If any exist, `generateBinder` writes a `<View>_StateBinder.java` next to the view: `connect(View v, PersistentState s)` calling `v.<field>.bind(s, "<field>")`. Runtime `PersistentState.connect(view)` finds it by the `<Class>_StateBinder` naming convention.

So it already walks **every `View` implementation** in any module that runs it — the natural hook for constructor enforcement (see Q below).

## Plan

### A. Convert all five parameterized custom views to the configurator (3: raw+signal where sensible)

Each becomes `implements View, Configurable<X.Config>` (+ `ChildrenView` for `SectionCard`), with a nested `Config implements View.Config`, a **`private` constructor**, `public static ViewBuilder<X, Config> with(Consumer<Config>)`, `config()`, and `body()` reading from `config`:

- **`PlayerBar`** — `Config` holds 6 `WritableSignal` fields (`trackIndex/position/playing/volume/seekRequest/volumeRequest`); setters are **writable-signal-only** (like `Audio.Config` — a binding has no raw form).
- **`LibraryView`** — 4 `WritableSignal`s (`trackIndex/position/playing/seekRequest`).
- **`NowPlayingSidebar`** — 1 (`trackIndex`).
- **`TrackRowView`** — `track(Track)`, `index(int)` (raw, structural), + 4 `WritableSignal`s (`trackIndex/position/playing/seekRequest`).
- **`SectionCard`** — `title(String)` + **`title(Signal<String>)`** (a literal → both forms per the raw+signal rule) and `children(View…)` for the content (`content` is a child, not a value).

Call sites change:
- `MusicPlayerView`: `new LibraryView(...)` / `new PlayerBar(...)` / `new NowPlayingSidebar(...)` → `…with(c -> c…)` (the sidebar keeps its `.modifiers(Clipped.with())`).
- `LibraryView`: `new TrackRowView(track, i, …)` → `TrackRowView.with(r -> r.track(...).index(...)…)`.
- All 13 `new SectionCard(title, VStack…)` → `SectionCard.with(s -> s.title(...)).children(VStack…)`.
- Tests (`MusicPlayerViewTest`, `SeekControlTest`) unchanged (root/holders stay).
- Root/no-arg views (`MusicPlayerView`, `HomeView`, sections, `Sidebar`, `SplitNavDemo`) stay as-is (mounted `new` by hosts — not parameterized).

### B. Enforcement — one deliberate decision

To *prevent* (not just discourage) constructor use, extend the processor. Two rule variants:

- **Rule A — ban parameterized public constructors** (recommended): the processor's existing View walk additionally checks constructors and errors on any **public/protected constructor with ≥1 parameter**. No-arg roots (`MusicPlayerView` mounted as `new`) stay legal; the five conversions satisfy it. Implemented as a check in the same `process()` loop (`getEnclosedElements` → `CONSTRUCTOR` + `Modifier` scan), emitting `Diagnostic.Kind.ERROR` with the class name + offending signature.
- **Rule B — ban all non-private constructors**: every `View` must funnel through `with(...)` (even no-arg roots). Stronger, but forces `MusicPlayerView` & every no-arg composite off `new X()` (hosts `quarkus/spring` `newRoot()` + tests change too) — much larger blast radius.

Two sub-decisions for either rule:
1. **Placement:** reuse `PersistedProcessor` (single processor, but mixes State-wiring with authoring-policy) **vs.** a new small `ViewAuthoringProcessor` class in the same jar (separate concerns, one `annotationProcessorPaths` entry can list both). I lean **new processor**.
2. **Wiring:** wire it into `pathland-demo-views` now (that's the only module currently running any processor); other apps opt in by adding `annotationProcessorPaths` — documented in the processor's javadoc + a line in `AGENTS.md`.

### C. Verify
`mvn -o -q -pl pathland-view,pathland-demo-views test` (31 demo tests + 143 view tests), then full `mvn -o test` (482); the processor-generated binders for the converted views' parents (`MusicPlayerView`) are unaffected.

## Questions
1. **Rule A or B**? (I recommend A — matches "prevent parameterized-constructor use" without forcing root views off `new`.)
2. **New `ViewAuthoringProcessor` or fold into `PersistedProcessor`?**
3. Confirm enforcement as a **compile ERROR** (not warning) — that's the only real "prevent".
1: A. 2: 2 new ViewAuthoringProcessor 3: 3: yes
1: A. 2: new ViewAuthoringProcessor 3: 3: yes

Everything is confirmed and researched. Here's the finalized plan.

## Final plan: configurator pattern for demo custom views + constructor enforcement

### 1. Convert the five parameterized custom views (`pathland-demo-views`)

Each becomes `implements View, Configurable<X.Config>`, with a nested `Config implements View.Config`, a **`private` constructor**, `public static ViewBuilder<X, Config> with(Consumer<Config>)`, `config()`, and `body()`/`render` reading from `config`:

| View | `Config` members |
|------|------------------|
| `PlayerBar` | 6 `WritableSignal`: `trackIndex/position/playing/volume/seekRequest/volumeRequest` |
| `LibraryView` | 4 `WritableSignal`: `trackIndex/position/playing/seekRequest` |
| `NowPlayingSidebar` | 1 `WritableSignal`: `trackIndex` |
| `TrackRowView` | raw `track(Track)`, `index(int)` + 4 `WritableSignal`s |
| `SectionCard` | `title(String)` **+ `title(Signal<String>)`** (raw+signal — Q3) + implements `ChildrenView` (`content` becomes `.children(...)`) |

- Setters for bindings are **writable-signal-only** (like `Audio.Config`); only `SectionCard.title` gets a raw+signal pair.
- Call sites: `MusicPlayerView` (`LibraryView`/`PlayerBar`/`NowPlayingSidebar` → `.with(c -> …)`; sidebar keeps `.with(Clipped.with())` on the result), `LibraryView` loop (`TrackRowView` → `.with(r -> …)`), all **13** `new SectionCard(title, VStack…)` → `SectionCard.with(s -> s.title(…)).children(VStack…)`.
- Unaffected: root/no-arg views (`MusicPlayerView`, `HomeView`, sections, `Sidebar`, `SplitNavDemo`) keep `new` mounts; `SeekControl`/`VolumeControl`/`PercentSeek` are signals, not views; `PlayerControlsStyle` is a `Style`.
- Behavior identical (config holds the same signals — emission unchanged).

### 2. New `ViewAuthoringProcessor` (Rule A, compile ERROR)

- New class `com.pathland.processor.ViewAuthoringProcessor` in `pathland-view-processor`:
  - Walks `roundEnv.getRootElements()` for classes assignable to `View` (same erasure technique as `PersistedProcessor`).
  - For each **non-abstract** such class, scans `getEnclosedElements()` for `CONSTRUCTOR`s; if any is `PUBLIC`/`PROTECTED` **and has ≥1 parameter** → `Diagnostic.Kind.ERROR` naming the class + offending signature, with a message steering to `with(Consumer<X.Config>)` (spec DSL.md §2).
  - No-arg constructors (roots) and abstract classes pass (abstract can't be instantiated; exempts developer base-view patterns).
  - Guards on `View` being on the classpath; returns `false` (processing continues).
- Register in `META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor` (second line next to `PersistedProcessor`) — consumers listing the jar in `annotationProcessorPaths` get both automatically.
- Wire: already in effect for `pathland-demo-views` (its `annotationProcessorPaths` points at the jar). The processor runs only on root classes being compiled in that module, so library/jar views are never flagged; library views already follow the private-ctor convention.

### 3. Docs
- One line in `AGENTS.md` (custom-view section): custom `View`s are configured via `with(Consumer<Config>)`; `ViewAuthoringProcessor` errors on parameterized public constructors (opt-in per module via `annotationProcessorPaths`).
- Update `pathland-view-processor/pom.xml` description (mentions both processors).

### 4. Verification
1. `cd lib/java && mvn -o -q -pl pathland-view test` → 143.
2. `mvn -o -q -pl pathland-demo-views -am test` → 31 (processor jar builds first; demo-views compiles **with** the new enforcement — proves the five conversions satisfy it).
3. Full `mvn -o test` → 482 (behavior-identical check across emitter/renderers).

<content>
148: ### The three operations
149: 
150: Every concrete view exposes the same three operations. They form one fluent
151: **builder**: any of the three may be the first call, and they may be chained in
152: any order. A later call overrides an earlier value for the same property.
153: 
154: | Operation | Purpose | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) |
155: |-----------|---------|----------------------------|
156: | **values** | Configure structural/layout values and a control's bound value | `View(config:)` — labels in the constructor |
157: | **modifiers** | Apply `ViewModifier` values, innermost-first | `.modifier(_:)` / `.padding(_:)` / … |
158: | **children** | Supply the content subtree (content-bearing views only) | trailing closure `{ … }` |
159: 
160: The **canonical builder spelling** (the recommended form; per-language spellings
161: are in [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)) is:
162: 
163: ```
164: ViewName.with { values }              // values   — a config-builder lambda
165:       .modifiers(modifier, ...)       // modifiers — varargs
166:       .children(view, ...)            // children  — varargs, content-bearing views only
167: ```
168: 
169: Any of the three may start the chain, e.g. all of these are equivalent:
170: 
171: ```
172: VStack.with { v in v.spacing(8) }.children(a, b).modifiers(m)
173: VStack.children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }.modifiers(m)
174: VStack.modifiers(m).children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }
175: ```
176: 
177: **Values are a config-builder lambda.** `with { c in … }` populates a per-view
178: fluent **config** (`VStack.Config`, `Text.Config`, …). It is the *same type* a
179: style's `makeBody(Config)` receives ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
180: The builder is **fluent and mutable**: setters return the config. Config-less
181: views (`Divider`, `Spacer`) take an empty `with()`.
182: 
183: **Every value member is reactive-capable (MUST).** A config member that carries a
184: value exposes **two forms** — a raw value and a `Signal<T>`:
185: 
186: ```
187: Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))            ≡  Text.with(t -> t.text(constant("hi")))
188: Visible.with(v -> v.visible(flagSignal))      // reactive visibility
189: Frame.with(f -> f.width(widthSignal))         // reactive sizing, layout included
190: ```
191: 
192: The **raw form is sugar for a constant signal**; a **non-constant** signal
193: becomes a **node-level binding** — a change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT`
194: / `SET_PROPERTY`, and a constant emits as a plain property with **zero binding
195: overhead**. This holds for *every* value member, layout included
196: (`spacing`, `alignment`, `padding`, `frame`, `columns`, …): anything describable
197: in the protocol can animate. A control's two-way *value* takes a
198: `WritableSignal<T>`; every other member takes a one-way `Signal<T>`.
199: 
200: **Per-language realization.** Java cannot declare a static and an instance
201: method with the same signature, so the Java realization holds the three
202: statically on the view class and exposes the chainable forms on the returned
203: builder/view type. Other languages map the operations to their idioms
204: (extension methods, associated functions + traits, package constructors +
205: methods, kwargs) — see [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).
206: 
207: Per-language adaptation summary:
208: 
209: | Language | Case | Composition mechanism | Example |
210: |----------|------|-----------------------|---------|
211: | SwiftUI | `camelCase` | trailing closures + result builder | `VStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 8) { Text("x").padding(16) }` |
212: | Java (`com.pathland.view`) | `camelCase` | `with(Consumer)` builder + `modifiers(...)` + `children(...)` | `VStack.with(v -> v.spacing(8)).children(Text.with(t -> t.text("x")).modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))))` |
213: | Rust (`pathland-view`) | `snake_case` | assoc fn + `ViewExt` trait + macros | `vstack![text("x").modifiers(Padding(16.0))]` |
214: 
215: ---
216: 
217: ## 3. State model (signals)
218: 
219: Pathland state is **Angular-style signals**. This is the non-negotiable
220: reactive core every DSL exposes.

I have what I need. Here's the analysis and proposed plan.

## The core question: can it be *generic*?

In Java, **no single generic method** can produce `Text.with("x")`, `Padding.with(24)`, `FontSize.with(18f)`:
- statics are not inherited/polymorphic, so each type needs its own declared overload;
- there's no way to discover a Config's "primary" member without a convention.

So "generic" resolves to two things:
1. **A spec convention** (define it once in `DSL.md`): *a view/modifier whose Config designates a single primary value member exposes `with(value)` and `with(Signal<T>)` overloads that are pure sugar for `with(c -> c.<primary>(value))`.*
2. **A uniform implementation pattern**: each overload is a **one-liner delegating to the existing `with(Consumer<Config>)`** — no new infrastructure, no codegen (the library is deliberately hand-written per AGENTS.md).

Example implementation (mechanical, per eligible type):
```java
// view — primary text
public static ViewBuilder<Text, Config> with(String text)        { return with(t -> t.text(text)); }
public static ViewBuilder<Text, Config> with(Signal<String> text){ return with(t -> t.text(text)); }
// modifier — uniform padding
public static Padding with(float uniform)                        { return with(p -> p.uniform(uniform)); }
```
Overloads are safe: `String`/`float`/`Signal<T>` never collide with `Consumer<Config>`; a `ViewBuilder` (chainable) is returned for views, the modifier value for modifiers. Only edge case: `X.with(null)` becomes ambiguous (acceptable).

## What qualifies as "primary" (designated, not "only")

- **Single-member** configs are obvious: `Text.text`, `Image.source`, `FontSize.size`, `ForegroundStyle.color`, `CornerRadius.radius`, `Opacity.value`, …
- **Multi-member but clearly-primary** — the spec names the designated member: `Padding.uniform` (`with(24)` ⇒ uniform), `Label.title`, `ProgressView.value`, `RoundedRectangle.cornerRadius`, `Audio/Video.source`, `NavigationLink.label`? (uncertain).
- **Multi-axis, ambiguous** ⇒ **no shortcut**, lambda only: `VStack`(alignment+spacing), `Offset`/`Position`(x,y), `FixedSize`(h,v), `Grid`(columns/rows/tracks), `Gauge`(v/min/max), `AspectRatio`(ratio+mode), `Slider/Toggle/TextField`(value + range/label), `Border`(color+width+radius), `Shadow`(color+radius+x+y).

## Proposed eligible list (please adjust)

**Views:** `Text`, `Image`, `Icon`, `Label`, `ProgressView`, `RoundedRectangle` (+ `Shape.with(ShapeKind)`?).
**Modifiers:** `Padding`(uniform), `FontSize`, `ForegroundStyle`, `Background`, `Tint`, `CornerRadius`, `Opacity`, `Blur`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect`, `LineLimit`, `Shadow`(radius?), `Kerning`, `Tracking`, `BaselineOffset`, `LineSpacing`, `FontWidth`, `FontFamily`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `LayoutPriority`, `ZIndex`, `ColorMultiply`, `ClipShape`, `HueRotation`, `Saturation`, `Contrast`, `Brightness`, `Grayscale`, `AccessibilityLabel`, `AccessibilityRole`, `AccessibilityState`, `ImageSource`, `Visible`, `Disabled`, `AllowsHitTesting`, `Underline`/`Strikethrough`(enabled), `PointerEvents`, `TapGesture`.

Most of these already have an `of(value)` doing exactly this — so there's a **consolidation decision** (below).

## DSL.md changes

Add a subsection under **§2 (The three operations)** — *Single-value shortcuts*:
- Rule: eligible types expose `with(value)` / `with(Signal<T>)` ≡ `with(c -> c.<primary>(value))`; byte-identical emission (source-surface only), tie into the §Conformance note.
- State the **designated-primary** concept and the exclusion for multi-axis configs.
- Add a small eligible-type table (view/modifier → primary member), and a couple of examples (`Text.with("hi")`, `Padding.with(16)`).
- Update the language-adaptation table (§2 / §9.3) and the §10 SwiftUI↔DSL map rows to show the shortcut as the Java spelling alongside the lambda.

## Questions before I draft the exact spec + code plan

1. **Scope:** the eligible list above — trim or extend? In particular: include the multi-member-but-primary ones (`Padding`, `Label`, `ProgressView`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Audio/Video.source`), or restrict to strict single-member configs only?
2. **`of(...)` fate:** (a) keep `of` and just add `with` aliases; (b) add `with`, **deprecate** `of`; (c) make `with(value)` canonical and **remove** `of`. (Note: `ProgressView.of(-1)`/`indeterminate()` and `RoundedRectangle.of` carry special semantics.)
3. **Generic vs explicit:** confirm you accept "spec convention + hand-written one-line delegating overloads" (recommended, matches the no-codegen stance) rather than an annotation-processor/codegen approach.
4. Should the shortcut also cover **enum-as-modifier** types (e.g. `FontWeight.BOLD` is already the value — no `with` needed) — I assume no.
5. Do you want a **shared helper** (e.g. a package-private static) to keep the overload bodies uniform, or is a direct `return with(c -> …)` one-liner per type fine?

I now have the full inventory. Here's the plan.

# Plan: single-value `with(...)` shortcuts + retire `.of(...)`

## A. Spec — `spec/DSL.md`

**1. New subsection under §2 (after "Every value member is reactive-capable"):**

> **Single-value shortcuts.** A view or modifier whose `Config` designates a **primary value member** exposes additional `with(...)` overloads that are pure sugar for the config-builder lambda:
> ```
> Text.with("hi")            ≡  Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))
> Padding.with(16)           ≡  Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))
> FontSize.with(sizeSignal)  ≡  FontSize.with(s -> s.size(sizeSignal))
> ```
> Both the raw and `Signal<T>` forms exist (raw = constant sugar, per §2). A shortcut emits **byte-identical** opcodes (source-surface only — §Conformance). Configs with no unambiguous primary (multi-axis: `Offset`/`Position` x,y; `FixedSize` h,v; `Grid` columns/rows/tracks; `Gauge` value/min/max; `Border` color+width(+radius); `Slider`/`Toggle`/`Picker` value+range) get **no** shortcut — use the lambda. Shortcuts are **additive sugar**: the `with(Consumer<Config>)` form is always canonical and sufficient.

**2. Eligible table** (view/modifier → designated primary):

| Kind | Shortcut |
|------|----------|
| Views | `Text(text)`, `Image(source)`, `Icon(name)`, `Label(title)`, `ProgressView(value)`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius)`, `Audio(source)`, `Video(source)` |
| Modifiers | `Padding(uniform)`, `FontSize`, `ForegroundStyle(color)`, `Background(color)`, `Tint(color)`, `CornerRadius`, `Opacity`, `Blur`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect(value)`, `LineLimit`, `Kerning`, `Tracking`, `BaselineOffset`, `LineSpacing`, `FontWidth`, `FontFamily`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `LayoutPriority`, `ZIndex`, `ColorMultiply(color)`, `ClipShape(shape)`, `HueRotation`, `Saturation`, `Contrast`, `Brightness`, `Grayscale`, `AccessibilityLabel(text)`, `AccessibilityRole(role)`, `AccessibilityState(state)`, `ImageSource(source)`, `Visible`, `Disabled`, `AllowsHitTesting`, `Underline(on)`, `Strikethrough(on)`, `PointerEvents(mask)`, `TapGesture(action)`, `Shadow(radius)` |

**3.** Update §9.3 language table + §10 SwiftUI map so Java shows the shortcut alongside the lambda.

## B. Library — shared helper + shortcuts

**1. New package-private helper `com.pathland.view.Configurators`:**
```java
final class Configurators {
    /** A view shortcut: build a fresh Config, apply the setter, wrap in a ViewBuilder. */
    static <V extends View & Configurable<C>, C extends View.Config> ViewBuilder<V, C> view(
            Supplier<C> config, Function<C, V> ctor, Consumer<C> setter) {
        C c = config.get();
        setter.accept(c);
        return new ViewBuilder<>(ctor.apply(c));
    }
    /** A modifier shortcut: build a fresh Config, apply the setter, construct the modifier. */
    static <M, C> M modifier(Supplier<C> config, Function<C, M> ctor, Consumer<C> setter) {
        C c = config.get();
        setter.accept(c);
        return ctor.apply(c);
    }
}
```
(Package-private; `Text::new`/`Padding::new` private-ctor method refs are legal within their own class.)

**2. Each eligible type gets the raw + signal overloads** delegating through the helper, e.g.:
```java
public static ViewBuilder<Text, Config> with(String text)         { return Configurators.view(Config::new, Text::new, c -> c.text(text)); }

# Plan: single-value `with(...)` shortcuts + retire `.of(...)`

## A. Spec — `spec/DSL.md`

**1. New §2 subsection "Single-value shortcuts"** (after the reactive-capable rule):

> A view/modifier whose `Config` designates a **primary value member** also exposes `with(primaryValue)` and `with(Signal<T>)` overloads — pure sugar for the lambda:
> ```
> Text.with("hi")            ≡  Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))
> Padding.with(16)           ≡  Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))
> FontSize.with(sizeSignal)  ≡  FontSize.with(s -> s.size(sizeSignal))
> ```
> **Multi-member configs get no shortcut** — a multi-value member (`Padding.edges(t,r,b,l)`, `Offset` x+y, `Gauge` value/min/max, `Border`, `FixedSize`, `AspectRatio`, control ranges) always uses the config lambda. Shortcuts are additive sugar; the `with(Consumer<Config>)` form stays canonical. Emission is byte-identical (source-surface only, §Conformance).

**2. Eligible table** (view/modifier → primary):

| Kind | Shortcut |
|------|----------|
| Views | `Text(text)`, `Image(source)`, `Icon(name)`, `Label(title)`, `ProgressView(value)`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius)`, `Audio(source)`, `Video(source)` |
| Modifiers | `Padding(uniform)`, `FontSize`, `ForegroundStyle(color)`, `Background(color)`, `Tint(color)`, `CornerRadius`, `Opacity`, `Blur`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect(value)`, `LineLimit`, `Kerning`, `Tracking`, `BaselineOffset`, `LineSpacing`, `FontWidth`, `FontFamily`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `LayoutPriority`, `ZIndex`, `ColorMultiply(color)`, `ClipShape(shape)`, `HueRotation`, `Saturation`, `Contrast`, `Brightness`, `Grayscale`, `AccessibilityLabel(text)`, `AccessibilityRole(role)`, `AccessibilityState(state)`, `ImageSource(source)`, `Visible`, `Disabled`, `AllowsHitTesting`, `Underline(on)`, `Strikethrough(on)`, `PointerEvents(mask)`, `TapGesture(action)`, `Shadow(radius)` |

**3.** Add a short note in §4/§5 referring to the shortcut; update §9.3 + §10 Java spellings.

## B. Library — shared helper + shortcuts

**1. New package-private `com.pathland.view.Configurators`:**
```java
final class Configurators {
    static <V extends View & Configurable<C>, C extends View.Config> ViewBuilder<V, C> view(
            Supplier<C> config, Function<C, V> ctor, Consumer<C> setter) {
        C c = config.get(); setter.accept(c); return new ViewBuilder<>(ctor.apply(c));
    }
    static <M, C> M modifier(Supplier<C> config, Function<C, M> ctor, Consumer<C> setter) {
        C c = config.get(); setter.accept(c); return ctor.apply(c);
    }
}
```

**2. Each eligible type** gains raw + signal overloads delegating through it:
```java
public static ViewBuilder<Text, Config> with(String text)         { return Configurators.view(Config::new, Text::new, c -> c.text(text)); }
public static ViewBuilder<Text, Config> with(Signal<String> text) { return Configurators.view(Config::new, Text::new, c -> c.text(text)); }
```
Modifiers return the modifier value via `Configurators.modifier(...)`.

**Remove every view/modifier construction `.of(...)`** (~70 classes). Migration rules:
- **Single-value** → `with(value)` shortcut (e.g. `Text.of(x)`→`Text.with(x)`, `Opacity.of(v)`→`Opacity.with(v)`).

Add empty `with()` where a config-less view lacks it (`Rectangle`/`Circle`/`Capsule`/`Ellipse`/`Divider`/`Spacer`); config-less modifiers already have it.
- **Multi-arg** (`Padding.of(t,r,b,l)`, `Offset.of(x,y)`, `Position.of(x,y)`, `AspectRatio.of(ratio,mode)`, `FixedSize.of(h,v)`, `Gauge.of(v,min,max)`, `Shadow.of(color,r,x,y)`, `Border.of(...)`, `Slider.of(...)`, `Toggle.of(...)`, `TextField.of(...)`, `TextEditor.of(...)`, `DatePicker.of(...)`, `ColorPicker.of(...)`, `Picker.of(...)`, `Menu.of(...)`, `Button.of(...)`, `Label.of(...)` combos, structural `VStack/HStack/ZStack/Grid/GridRow/Group/ScrollView/Lazy*.of(...)`, `Audio/Video.of(...)`, `Frame.of(...)/ofWidth/ofHeight`) → **removed**; callers use the lambda / `.children(...)` / the shortcut as applicable.

**Keep** (data/factory functions, not builder-surface construction):

- `SizeThatFits.of(...)` (structural slot, no `with(Consumer)`) → `SizeThatFits.with(View...)` / `with(Fit...)`.

**Call-site migration** (tests + demos): `Frame.of*`/`Frame.ofWidth`/`ofHeight` → `Frame.with(f -> …)`; the handful of `Rectangle.of()` etc. → `with()`; `SizeThatFits.of` → `with`. (Demos already use `with`/`children`/`modifiers` almost everywhere.)

# Final plan: single-value `with(...)` shortcuts + retire all `.of(...)` construction factories

## A. Spec — `spec/DSL.md`

**1. New §2 subsection "Single-value shortcuts"** (after the reactive-capable rule):

> A view/modifier whose `Config` designates a **primary value member** also exposes `with(primaryValue)` / `with(Signal<T>)` overloads — pure sugar for the lambda:
> ```
> Text.with("hi")            ≡  Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))
> Padding.with(16)           ≡  Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))
> FontSize.with(sizeSignal)  ≡  FontSize.with(s -> s.size(sizeSignal))
> ```
> **Multi-member configs get no shortcut** — a multi-value member (`Padding.edges`, `Offset` x+y, `Gauge`, `Border`, `FixedSize`, `AspectRatio`, control ranges) always uses the config lambda. Shortcuts are additive sugar; `with(Consumer<Config>)` stays canonical; emission is byte-identical (source-surface, §Conformance).

**2. Eligible table** (view/modifier → primary):

| Kind | Shortcut |
|------|----------|
| Views | `Text(text)`, `Image(source)`, `Icon(name)`, `Label(title)`, `ProgressView(value)`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius)`, `Audio(source)`, `Video(source)` |
| Modifiers | `Padding(uniform)`, `FontSize`, `ForegroundStyle(color)`, `Background(color)`, `Tint(color)`, `CornerRadius`, `Opacity`, `Blur`, `Rotation`, `ScaleEffect(value)`, `LineLimit`, `Kerning`, `Tracking`, `BaselineOffset`, `LineSpacing`, `FontWidth`, `FontFamily`, `MinimumScaleFactor`, `LayoutPriority`, `ZIndex`, `ColorMultiply(color)`, `ClipShape(shape)`, `HueRotation`, `Saturation`, `Contrast`, `Brightness`, `Grayscale`, `AccessibilityLabel(text)`, `AccessibilityRole(role)`, `AccessibilityState(state)`, `ImageSource(source)`, `Visible`, `Disabled`, `AllowsHitTesting`, `Underline(on)`, `Strikethrough(on)`, `PointerEvents(mask)`, `TapGesture(action)`, `Shadow(radius)` |

**3. Update §9.3 + §10** Java spellings to show the shortcut; tighten §5.7/§8 wording (`.of(...)` gone; style factories use `with`).

## B. Library — shared helper + shortcuts

**1. New package-private `com.pathland.view.Configurators`:**
```java
final class Configurators {
    static <V extends View & Configurable<C>, C extends View.Config> ViewBuilder<V,C> view(
            Supplier<C> config, Function<C,V> ctor, Consumer<C> setter) { C c=config.get(); setter.accept(c); return new ViewBuilder<>(ctor.apply(c)); }
    static <M,C> M modifier(Supplier<C> config, Function<C,M> ctor, Consumer<C> setter)        { C c=config.get(); setter.accept(c); return ctor.apply(c); }
}
```

**2. Eligible types** gain raw + signal overloads delegating through it:
```java
public static ViewBuilder<Text,Config> with(String text)         { return Configurators.view(Config::new, Text::new, c -> c.text(text)); }
public static ViewBuilder<Text,Config> with(Signal<String> text) { return Configurators.view(Config::new, Text::new, c -> c.text(text)); }
```
Modifiers return the modifier value via `Configurators.modifier(...)`. Overloads never collide with `with(Consumer<Config>)` (only `X.with(null)` is ambiguous — accepted).

## C. Retire every `.of(...)` construction factory (option c)

**Remove** across all view/modifier classes (~70). Migration:
- **Single-value** → `with(value)` shortcut.
- **Config-less no-arg** (`Rectangle/Circle/Capsule/Ellipse/Divider/Spacer.of()`, `Clipped/ColorInvert/Hidden/Italic/ScaledToFit/ScaledToFill/Underline/Strikethrough.of()`) → **empty `with()`** (add empty `with()` to shapes/Divider/Spacer where missing; config-less modifiers already have it). *(No current usages — safe.)*
- **Multi-arg** (`Padding.of(t,r,b,l)`, `Offset/Position.of(x,y)`, `AspectRatio.of`, `FixedSize.of`, `Gauge.of`, `Shadow.of`, `Border.of`, `Slider/Toggle/TextField/TextEditor/DatePicker/ColorPicker/Picker/Menu/Button/Label/Audio/Video.of`, structural `VStack/HStack/ZStack/Grid/GridRow/Group/ScrollView/Lazy*.of`, `Frame.of`/`ofWidth`/`ofHeight`) → **removed**; callers use lambda / `.children(...)` / shortcut.

**Styles (prune per your call):**
- `BorderedButtonStyle.of()` + `of(padding,background,borderColor,radius)` → removed (dead); add `BorderedButtonStyle.with(b -> b.padding(..).background(..).borderColor(..).radius(..))` returning the style value, with a nested `Config` + private constructor; keep `INSTANCE`.
- App-authored `PlayerControlsStyle.of(...)` → `PlayerControlsStyle.with(p -> p.trackIndex(..)…)` (nested `Config`).
- Keep enum constants `PlainButtonStyle.INSTANCE`, `NativeAudioStyle/VideoStyle.INSTANCE`, `Default/TitleOnly/IconOnly LabelStyle.INSTANCE`.

**Keep** (data/branch factories, not the builder surface): `Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Conditional.when` / `Case.of` / `Case.otherwise`, `Fit.of`, `Signals.*`, `EnvironmentKey.of`, `Route.of`, `Params.of`, `EnvironmentData.of`. Convert `SizeThatFits.of(...)` → `SizeThatFits.with(View...)` / `with(Fit...)`.

**Special cases:** `AccessibilityRole.of(int)` reserved-code validation moves into `AccessibilityRole.with(int)`; `HtmlRendererTest`'s `assertThrows` migrates to `with(20)`.

**Call-site migration:** `Frame.of*`/`ofWidth`/`ofHeight` (12 sites) → `Frame.with(f -> …)`; `AccessibilityRole.of` → `with`; `SizeThatFits.of`/`Fit.of` per above; `PlayerControlsStyle.of` → `with`. Demos otherwise already use `with`/`children`/`modifiers`.

**Per-language realization.** Java cannot declare a static and an instance
method with the same signature, so the Java realization holds the three
statically on the view class and exposes the chainable forms on the returned
builder/view type. Other languages map the operations to their idioms
(extension methods, associated functions + traits, package constructors +
methods, kwargs) — see [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).

**Single-value shortcuts.** A view or modifier whose config designates a
**primary value member** MAY also expose `with(value)` / `with(Signal<T>)`
overloads that are pure sugar for the config-builder lambda:

```
Text.with("hi")            ≡  Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))
Padding.with(16)           ≡  Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))
FontSize.with(sizeSignal)  ≡  FontSize.with(s -> s.size(sizeSignal))
```

A shortcut emits **byte-identical** opcodes and carries no extra semantics
(source-surface only — [§Conformance](#conformance)). The config-lambda form
(`with(c -> …)`) remains canonical and always sufficient.

- **Only a designated primary member** gets a shortcut. A config with **several
  equivalent members** (`Padding` edges, `Offset`/`Position` x+y, `Gauge`
  value/min/max, `Border` color+width(+radius), `FixedSize` horizontal+vertical,
  `AspectRatio` ratio+mode, a control's value+range) has **no** shortcut — use the
  lambda. `Padding` is the exception that proves it: its single-value primary is
  `uniform`, and per-edge padding is the lambda.
- **Both forms exist where the member has both**: a raw value and a
  `Signal<T>` (same rule as the config setters above). A two-way control value is
  never a shortcut — it stays a `WritableSignal` config member.
- The Java realization declares the overloads per type (Java statics are not
  inherited); they delegate to the existing `with(Consumer<Config>)` factory, so
  there is exactly one construction path. The former `.of(...)` factories are
  **removed** — a shortcut (or the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty `with()` for
  config-less views) replaces every one.

Eligible members (non-exhaustive; the companion tables list the surface):

| Kind | Shortcut |
|------|----------|
| Views | `Text(text)`, `Image(source)`, `Icon(name)`, `Label(title)`, `ProgressView(value)`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius)`, `Audio(source)`, `Video(source)`, `Shape(kind)` |
| Modifiers | `Padding(uniform)`, `FontSize(size)`, `ForegroundStyle(color)`, `Background(color)`, `Tint(color)`, `CornerRadius(radius)`, `Opacity(value)`, `Blur(radius)`, `Rotation(degrees)`, `ScaleEffect(value)`, `LineLimit(value)`, `Kerning`/`Tracking`/`BaselineOffset`/`LineSpacing`/`FontWidth`/`MinimumScaleFactor`/`LayoutPriority`/`ZIndex`(value), `FontFamily(family)`, `HueRotation(degrees)`, `Saturation`/`Contrast`/`Brightness`/`Grayscale`(value), `ColorMultiply(color)`, `ClipShape(shape)`, `AccessibilityLabel(text)`, `AccessibilityRole(role)`, `AccessibilityState(state)`, `Shadow(radius)`, `ImageSource(source)`, `Visible`/`Disabled`/`AllowsHitTesting`(bool), `Underline`/`Strikethrough`(bool), `PointerEvents(mask)`, `TapGesture(action)` |

- **Custom views and styles use the configurator** (spec DSL.md §2): an
  app-authored `View` with values implements `Configurable<View.Config>`, holds a
  **`private` constructor**, and exposes
  `static ViewBuilder<View, Config> with(Consumer<Config>)`; a style
  (`ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle`/`AudioStyle`/`VideoStyle`) expose
  `static X with(Consumer<Config>)` returning the style value (e.g.
  `BorderedButtonStyle.with(b -> b.padding(..).background(..)…)`). Creation goes
  through the configurator, never a parameterized constructor. The
  `pathland-view-processor` `ViewAuthoringProcessor` **errors** on
  public/protected constructors **with parameters** in custom `View` **and**
  `Style` implementations (no-arg roots and abstract types are exempt), so the
  convention is compile-enforced where the processor is wired
  (`annotationProcessorPaths`). The library's own views/styles follow the same
  shape (`Audio`, `Text`, `BorderedButtonStyle`, …).
- **SwiftUI-style `body()`**: composite views declare `View body()` (their subtree);
  the library's primitives override `render(Environment)` to materialize a
  `PathlandNode`. `body()` is evaluated **once at mount** — reactive values come from
  signals (`Text.with(t -> t.text(Signal))`, `Signals.computed`), not from body
  re-evaluation, so the emitter keeps its fine-grained `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY` deltas.
- **The three operations (spec DSL.md §2)**: every concrete view exposes
  `with(Consumer<Config>)` (values) / `.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` / `.children(View...)`
  chainable in **any order** on a returned `ViewBuilder` (Java's static-vs-instance
  rule: the statics sit on the view class, the chain on the builder). Values are a
  fluent per-view `Config` (`VStack.with(v -> v.alignment(...).spacing(8))`,
  `Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))`); modifiers are `ViewModifier` values
  (`Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))`) or — for single values — the value itself
  (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, a `ButtonStyle`). The `View` interface has
  **no per-modifier sugar** (`font`/`navigate`/`environment`/`onPathChange` were
  removed — use `.modifiers(Font…)`, `.modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate(…))`,
  `.modifiers(EnvironmentBinding.with(e -> e.key(…).value(…)))`,
  `.modifiers(PathChange.with(p -> p.listener(…)))`), and the `*Mod` shims
  (`EnvironmentMod`→`EnvironmentBinding`, `router/NavigationMod`→`NavigationIntent`,
  `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed**.
- **Single-value shortcuts (spec DSL.md §2)**: a view/modifier whose config has a
  designated primary member also exposes `with(value)` / `with(Signal<T>)` overloads
  that are pure sugar for the lambda — `Text.with("hi")`, `Padding.with(16)`,
  `FontSize.with(sizeSignal)`. Multi-member configs (`Padding.edges`, `Offset`,
  `Gauge`, `Border`, …) have **no** shortcut — use the lambda. The shortcut delegates
  to the same `with(Consumer<Config>)` factory via the package-private
  `Configurators` helper (one construction path). The former `.of(...)` construction
  factories are **removed** — a shortcut (or the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty
  `with()` for config-less views) replaces every one. Only data/branch factories keep
  `of`: `Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Case.of`, `Fit.of`, `EnvironmentKey.of`,
  `Route.of`, `Params.of`, `Signals.*`.
  Sizing is the `Frame` modifier value
  (`Frame.with(f -> f.width(w).height(h).alignment(..))` and the lambda
  configurator `Frame.with(f -> f.minWidth(..).maxWidth(..).alignment(..))`
  (min/ideal/max bounds)); all
  compile to the same `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/min-max `SET_PROPERTY`s.
  Typed enums
  (`Alignment`/`TextAlignment`/`FontWeight`/`Truncation`), not raw ints.

## Summary

**Shortcuts** (`spec/DSL.md` §2, new "Single-value shortcuts"): eligible views/modifiers expose `with(value)`/`with(Signal<T>)` sugar via the package-private `Configurators` helper — `Text.with("hi")`, `Padding.with(16)`, `FontSize.with(sizeSignal)`. content.text:
The demo main sources have ~180 single-setter lambda sites that now have shortcuts. Here's the plan.

## Plan: use the `with(value)` shortcuts throughout `pathland-demo-views` main

**Goal:** in `lib/java/pathland-demo-views/src/main/**`, convert every single-primary config lambda to the shortcut form, keeping multi-member/control lambdas. Purely cosmetic (shortcuts ≡ lambda — byte-identical), demo tests (31) must stay green.

**Convert** (single settable primary → `X.with(value)` / `X.with(signal)`):
- `Text.with(t -> t.text(…))` → `Text.with(…)` (incl. `computed(...)` → `Text.with(sig)`)
- `Image.with(i -> i.source(…))`, `Icon.with(i -> i.name(…))`, `Audio.with(a -> a.source(…))`, `Video.with(v -> v.source(…))`
- `Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(…))` → `Padding.with(…)`
- `FontSize.with(s -> s.size(…))`, `ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(…))`, `Background.with(b -> b.color(…))`
- `CornerRadius.with(c -> c.radius(…))`, `Opacity.with(o -> o.value(…))`, `Rotation.with(r -> r.degrees(…))`, `ScaleEffect.with(s -> s.value(…))`, `ZIndex.with(z -> z.value(…))`, `Kerning.with(k -> k.value(…))`, `Tracking.with(tr -> tr.value(…))`, `LineLimit.with(l -> l.value(…))`, `Shadow.with(s -> s.radius(…))`, `AllowsHitTesting.with(a -> a.allowed(…))`, `AccessibilityRole.with(a -> a.role(…))`, `Disabled.with(d -> d.disabled(…))`, etc.
- `AccessibilityRole.with(a -> a.role(Roles.HEADER))` → `AccessibilityRole.with(Roles.HEADER)` (int primary)
- Optional consistency win: **`SectionCard`** (demo custom view, `title` is its only primary) gains `SectionCard.with(String)` / `with(Signal<String>)` shortcuts so `SectionCard.with(s -> s.title(…)).children(…)` → `SectionCard.with(…).children(…)`. (Does not affect the multi-signal `PlayerBar`/`PlayerControlsStyle` — those stay `with(Consumer)` since they're multi-member.)

**Keep as-is** (multi-member / no primary / control semantics):
- `Padding.with(p -> p.edges(...))` (4-edge)
- `Border.with(b -> b.color(..).width(..).radius(..))`, `Shadow.with(s -> s.color(..).radius(..).x(..).y(..))`, `Offset.with(o -> o.x(..).y(..))`, `Gauge.with(g -> g.value(..).minValue(..).maxValue(..))`
- `Frame.with(f -> f.width(..).height(..))`
- `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Toggle`/`TextField`/`DatePicker`/`Picker`/`Menu`/`Button.action`/`Button.title` config lambdas (control values + ranges, `isOn`, `selection`, `placeholder`…)
- `Audio/Video` multi-source-config lambdas that set more than `source`

**Mechanics:** file-by-file edit (~25 files), preserving the issue-#140 chain order (modifiers → with → children) and indentation. No behavior change.

**Verify:** `mvn -o -q -pl pathland-demo-views test` (31), then full `mvn -o test` (green), restarting from the current branch `feat/with-shortcuts-retire-of` (`8ea5e91a`).

## Questions
1. Include the **`SectionCard.with(String)`** shortcut (I recommend yes — its `title` is the sole primary), or strictly convert only existing library shortcuts?
2. Scope confirmed as **demo-views main only** (demo tests have no such sites; library/starters/render-html/main are already migrated)?
1: yes 2: yes

Final plan confirmed.

## Plan: use `with(value)` shortcuts throughout demo-views main

**Branch:** `feat/with-shortcuts-retire-of` (`8ea5e91a`), files under `lib/java/pathland-demo-views/src/main/**` only.

**1. Telegram-style conversions** (~25 files, ~180 sites) — every single-primary config lambda → shortcut (raw or `Signal<T>`):
- `Text.with(t -> t.text(…))` → `Text.with(…)` (incl. `computed(...)`/signals)
- `Image.with(i -> i.source(…))`, `Icon.with(i -> i.name(…))`, `Audio.with(a -> a.source(…))`, `Video.with(v -> v.source(…))`
- `Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(…))`, `FontSize.with(s -> s.size(…))`, `ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(…))`, `Background.with(b -> b.color(…))`
- `CornerRadius.with(c -> c.radius(…))`, `Opacity.with(o -> o.value(…))`, `Rotation.with(r -> r.degrees(…))`, `ScaleEffect.with(s -> s.value(…))`, `ZIndex.with(z -> z.value(…))`, `Kerning.with(k -> k.value(…))`, `Tracking.with(tr -> tr.value(…))`, `LineLimit.with(l -> l.value(…))`, `Shadow.with(s -> s.radius(…))`, `AllowsHitTesting.with(a -> a.allowed(…))`, `Disabled.with(d -> d.disabled(…))`, `AccessibilityRole.with(a -> a.role(…))`, and any other eligible single-primary modifier in the table.

content.text:
Committed as `ac1c8224`.

## Summary

Applied the single-value `with(value)` shortcuts throughout `pathland-demo-views` main (~28 files, 236/226 churn):

- **Converted:** `Text.with(...)`, `Padding.with(...)`, `FontSize.with(...)`, `ForegroundStyle.with(...)`, `Background.with(...)`, `CornerRadius.with(...)`, `Opacity/ScaleEffect/ZIndex/Kerning/Tracking/LineLimit.with(...)`, `Rotation.with(...)`, `Shadow.with(...)`, `AllowsHitTesting.with(...)`, `AccessibilityRole.with(...)`, `Icon.with(...)`, `Image/Audio/Video.with(...)` — raw or `Signal<T>` as appropriate.
- **`SectionCard`** gained `with(String)`/`with(Signal<String>)` (its sole primary is `title`), so all 13 `SectionCard.with(s -> s.title(…))` sites became `SectionCard.with(…)`.
- **Kept as lambda** (multi-member/control): `Padding.edges`, `Border`, full `Shadow`, `Offset`, `Gauge`, `Frame`, `Slider`/`Stepper`/`Toggle`/`TextField`/`DatePicker`/`Picker`/`Menu`/`TextEditor`, `Button` actions.

**Verification:** demo-views 31 tests green; full Java reactor **492 tests green** — behavior unchanged (shortcuts ≡ lambdas, byte-identical).

## Objective
- Finish the DSL v2 migration: the Java/Rust authoring surface is `with`/`modifiers`/`children` + signals-first configs, single-value `with(value)` shortcuts are the replacement for the retired `.of(...)` factories, and the configurator convention (private constructors + `with(Consumer<Config>)`) is compile-enforced for custom views and styles.
- Current task: convert `pathland-demo-views` main sources to use the new shortcuts (e.g. `Padding.with(24)` instead of `Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(24))`), then verify and commit.

## Important Details
- Branch: `feat/with-shortcuts-retire-of` at `8ea5e91a` (based on `style/demo-chain-order` at `744ed7b9`; both branches unmerged. `main` is at `4466ecde`, which merged PR #139 up to `207befbf`.)
- Locked decisions (this session):
  - Issue #140: demo chain-order convention = `.modifiers(...)` first (single call, all modifiers), `.with(...)`, `.children(...)`, one op per line.
  - Custom views: `Configurable<Config>` + nested `Config` + **private** constructor + `static with(Consumer<Config>)`; `ViewAuthoringProcessor` errors on `public`/`protected` parameterized constructors in `View` **and** `Style` implementations (no-arg roots, abstract classes, enums, records, interfaces exempt). Opt-in per module via `annotationProcessorPaths` (only `pathland-demo-views` wires it).
  - Single-value `with(value)`/`with(Signal<T>)` shortcuts are pure sugar for the lambda; only a designated primary member gets one; multi-member configs (`Padding.edges`, `Offset`, `Gauge`, `Border`, `FixedSize`, `AspectRatio`, control ranges) stay lambda-only. Shared package-private `Configurators` helper (`view(...)`/`modifier(...)`).
  - `.of(...)` construction factories retired across library, styles, and demos. Kept only data/branch factories: `Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Case.of`, `Fit.of`, `EnvironmentKey.of`, `Route.of`, `Params.of`; styles now `with(...)` (e.g. `BorderedButtonStyle.with(b -> ...)`); `Frame.of*/ofWidth/ofHeight` → `Frame.with(f -> ...)`; `SizeThatFits.of` → `SizeThatFits.with`; no-arg config-less `.of()` → empty `with()`.
  - `AccessibilityRole.with(int)` now does the reserved-code validation.
- Verification state at `8ea5e91a`: Java view tests **148 green** (142 + `ShortcutTest` 6); full Java reactor **BUILD SUCCESS** (~492 via the double-counting awk); Rust `cargo test --workspace` green (339 tests, 30 suites); clippy warnings are pre-existing in `pathland-core`.

- Phases 0–2: signals-first spec, Java, and Rust (Rust `Reactive<T>`/`IntoReactive<T>`, `Bound` removed) — committed `416a88e1`, `ac39bb82`.

content.text:
You're right — that's an inconsistency. Here's my analysis:

**Findings**
- `ZStack.Config` has exactly one member: `alignment` (`ZStack.java:17-32`), so it qualifies for a `with(value)` shortcut per spec `DSL.md` §2 ("a view… whose config designates a **primary value member** MAY also expose `with(value)`/`with(Signal<T>)`"; only **several equivalent members** disqualify — `ZStack.java` has none).
- `VStack`/`HStack`/`LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack`/grids are multi-member (`alignment` + `spacing`, etc.) so they correctly have **no** shortcut.
- ZStack currently only exposes `with(Consumer<Config>)`, `modifiers(...)`, `children(...)` (`ZStack.java:43-57`).
- No overload ambiguity: `Alignment` (enum) and `Signal<Alignment>` are not `Consumer`, so `with(Alignment)` / `with(Signal<Alignment>)` coexist safely with `with(Consumer<Config>)` (same pattern as other shortcuts via the package-private `Configurators.view(...)` helper).
- Spec `DSL.md` documents ZStack only in the lambda form at §4.2 (`line 430`) and **does not list it** in the §2 eligible-members table (`line 240`).
- One demo site already uses the lambda form: `MusicPlayerView.java:94` — `ZStack.with(z -> z.alignment(Alignment.BOTTOM_CENTER))`.

**Plan**
1. `ZStack.java`: add
   - `public static ViewBuilder<ZStack, Config> with(Alignment alignment)`
   - `public static ViewBuilder<ZStack, Config> with(Signal<Alignment> alignment)`
   delegating to `Configurators.view(() -> new Config(), ZStack::new, c -> c.alignment(alignment))`.
2. `spec/DSL.md`: add `ZStack(alignment)` to the §2 eligible-members "Views" row and update the §4.2 ZStack row to note the shortcut.
3. `ShortcutTest.java`: add `zstackAlignmentShortcutEqualsLambda` (render `ZStack.with(Alignment.CENTER)` == `ZStack.with(z -> z.alignment(Alignment.CENTER))`, checking `Properties.ALIGNMENT`).
4. `MusicPlayerView.java:94`: switch to `ZStack.with(Alignment.BOTTOM_CENTER)` (demo consistency; `LayoutSection.java` uses no alignment so is unchanged).
5. Verify: `cd lib/java && mvn -o -pl pathland-view test` then full `mvn -o test`; update `lib/java/pathland-view/status.md` if it inventories shortcuts.

44:   `PathChangeMod`→`PathChange`, `FontWeightMod`→`FontWeight`, …) are **removed** —
45:   every consumer (demo views, starters, renderers) is on the v2 surface. The
46:   former `.of(...)` **construction factories are removed**: a **single-value
47:   `with(value)` / `with(Signal<T>)` shortcut** replaces them where the config has
48:   a designated primary member (`Text.with("hi")`, `Padding.with(16)`,
49:   `FontSize.with(sizeSignal)` — pure sugar for the lambda, via the package-private
50:   `Configurators` helper), and the lambda / `.children(...)` / empty `with()` (for
51:   config-less views) covers the rest. Only data/branch factories keep `of`
52:   (`Color.of/rgb/argb/token`, `Case.of`, `Fit.of`, `EnvironmentKey.of`, `Route.of`,
53:   `Params.of`). The `View` interface carries no per-modifier factory
54:   methods (spec `DSL.md` §5.6).
55: - **Signals-first configs (spec DSL.md §2)**: **every value member** exposes a raw
56:   setter (sugar for `Signals.constant`) and a `Signal<T>` setter — layout included
57:   (`spacing`, `alignment`, `padding`, `frame`, `columns`/`tracks`, …). A
58:   non-constant signal becomes a **node-level binding** (re-emits only that
59:   property); a constant carries zero binding overhead. Two-way control *values*
60:   take `WritableSignal<T>`; every other member takes a one-way `Signal<T>`
61:   (`WritableSignal extends Signal`). Views and modifiers place values through the

60: ---
61: 
62: ## 1. Design principles (DSL-flavored)
63: 
64: These recap the protocol's non-negotiables in author-facing terms. A conformant
65: DSL must be *shaped* by them:
66: 
67: - **Declarative structure, never positions.** The DSL expresses `WHAT` — a
68:   `VStack`, a `HStack`, a `Text` — and constraint properties (spacing, padding,
69:   alignment, size hints). It never computes bounds and never emits rects.
70: - **Exactly three authoring operations.** Every view exposes the same three
71:   operations — **configure values** (§5.0 `with`), **apply modifiers**
72:   (`modifiers`), and, for content-bearing views, **supply children**
73:   (`children`). The three are a single fluent builder: any of them may be the
74:   first call and they may be chained in **any order** (see
75:   [§2](#2-canonical-signature-notation)); a later call overrides an earlier
76:   value for the same property.
77: - **`body()` is evaluated once at mount.** A composite view declares its
78:   subtree once; reactivity comes from **signals**, never from re-evaluating the
79:   body. This is what lets the emitter produce fine-grained
80:   `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` deltas instead of rebuilding the tree.
81:   The one sanctioned exception is a **structural container**
82:   ([§3.4](#34-structural-reactivity-conditional-rendering)): its content is
83:   re-evaluated on a signal change and the emitter reconciles the retained
84:   subtree into `TREE` deltas.
85: - **Modifiers are decoupled from views — and never hard-bound to a view
86:   type.** Any modifier applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a
87:   `VStack` alike), and any developer can **author a custom modifier in
88:   application code** (a `ViewModifier`) that applies to any existing view —
89:   library primitive, container, control, custom view, or an already-modified
90:   view (see [§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)). A modifier a
91:   given renderer cannot apply is **allowed and ignored** — the property is
92:   still emitted.
93: - **There is exactly one modifier mechanism.** Built-in core modifiers are
94:   **not** a separate syntax: they are `ViewModifier` values the library ships,
95:   composed into a view through the shared `modifiers(...)` operation. There is
96:   **no per-modifier sugar on the view type** — `Padding` applied via
97:   `.modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16)))`. Core and application-authored
98:   modifiers share the same surface.
99: - **A modifier's type is named for the modifier it applies — never with a
100:   `Mod` suffix.** Where a modifier applies a single value (a font, a font
101:   weight, an alignment, a style), the value type itself MAY *be* the modifier
102:   (`FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.headline()`, `MyButtonStyle`), so there is one name
103:   for the concept. Languages that cannot merge the two (e.g. C#, whose enums
104:   cannot implement interfaces) use the equivalent value form. See
105:   [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules).
106: - **There is exactly one style mechanism.** A customizable control/view takes
107:   its **content** from a *style* value (`ButtonStyle`, `LabelStyle`,
108:   `AudioStyle`, `VideoStyle`, …) scoped through the environment; the control
109:   owns its native component + interaction and the style owns the content
110:   ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)). Closed-variant/token
111:   styles (`ToggleStyle`, `PickerStyle`, `TextStyle`) are the same surface.
112: - **Values vs modifiers.** Structural/layout parameters and a control's bound
113:   value (`alignment`, `spacing`, `text`, `isOn`, `selection`) are **values**
114:   configured through `with(...)`. Everything decorative (padding, color, font,
115:   frame, border, …) is a **modifier** applied through `modifiers(...)`.
116: - **`Color` is never a modifier.** `Color` has SwiftUI's dual identity: it is a
117:   **View** (a layout-greedy solid-color fill) and a **Data Type** (passed into
118:   style-taking modifiers: `.foregroundStyle`, `.background`, `.border`,
119:   `.tint`). There is **no** `.color()` modifier, and `.foregroundColor(_:)` is
120:   deprecated — foreground styling is always `.foregroundStyle(_:)`.
121: - **Only changes are transmitted.** Emission is diff-based; an unchanged tree
122:   emits **zero** opcodes. The DSL describes values; the emitter diffs them.
123: - **Typed enums, never raw ints.** Every enumerated value is a typed constant
124:   (`Alignment.leading`, `FontWeight.bold`, `ToggleStyle.checkbox`), not a bare
125:   integer. The numeric code is the DSL's job to resolve (see the value-type and
126:   enum tables in MODIFIERS.md).
127: 
128: ---
129: 
130: ## 2. Canonical signature notation
131: 
132: The canonical signatures below are written SwiftUI-shaped and language
133: agnostic. Conventions used:
134: 
135: - `View(config:)` / `T("…")` — a view/control constructed with its **values**.
136: - `{ ... }` — the child subtree (a trailing closure in SwiftUI; a vararg,
137:   macro, builder, or lambda in other languages).
138: - `Signal<T>` — a read-only derived or writable signal; `WritableSignal<T>` —
139:   a two-way binding target. A control takes a `WritableSignal<T>` for its
140:   value (see [§3](#3-state-model-signals)).
141: - `()` — the action a `Button` fires.
142: - `.modifier(m)` — apply a **modifier value** to a view; chainable on any
143:   view. Every modifier — built-in or application-authored — is such a value
144:   ([§5.6](#56-custom-modifiers-developer-authored)).
145: - Modifiers chain and are applied **innermost-first** (the last chained
146:   modifier's property wins).
147: 
148: ### The three operations
149: 
150: Every concrete view exposes the same three operations. They form one fluent
151: **builder**: any of the three may be the first call, and they may be chained in
152: any order. A later call overrides an earlier value for the same property.
153: 
154: | Operation | Purpose | Canonical (SwiftUI-shaped) |
155: |-----------|---------|----------------------------|
156: | **values** | Configure structural/layout values and a control's bound value | `View(config:)` — labels in the constructor |
157: | **modifiers** | Apply `ViewModifier` values, innermost-first | `.modifier(_:)` / `.padding(_:)` / … |
158: | **children** | Supply the content subtree (content-bearing views only) | trailing closure `{ … }` |
159: 
160: The **canonical builder spelling** (the recommended form; per-language spellings
161: are in [§9.3](#93-language-adaptation-rules)) is:
162: 
163: ```
164: ViewName.with { values }              // values   — a config-builder lambda
165:       .modifiers(modifier, ...)       // modifiers — varargs
166:       .children(view, ...)            // children  — varargs, content-bearing views only
167: ```
168: 
169: Any of the three may start the chain, e.g. all of these are equivalent:
170: 
171: ```
172: VStack.with { v in v.spacing(8) }.children(a, b).modifiers(m)
173: VStack.children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }.modifiers(m)
174: VStack.modifiers(m).children(a, b).with { v in v.spacing(8) }
175: ```
176: 
177: **Values are a config-builder lambda.** `with { c in … }` populates a per-view
178: fluent **config** (`VStack.Config`, `Text.Config`, …). It is the *same type* a
179: style's `makeBody(Config)` receives ([§5.7](#57-styleable-controls-the-style-contract)).
180: The builder is **fluent and mutable**: setters return the config. Config-less
181: views (`Divider`, `Spacer`) take an empty `with()`.
182: 
183: **Every value member is reactive-capable (MUST).** A config member that carries a
184: value exposes **two forms** — a raw value and a `Signal<T>`:
185: 
186: ```
187: Text.with(t -> t.text("hi"))            ≡  Text.with(t -> t.text(constant("hi")))
188: Visible.with(v -> v.visible(flagSignal))      // reactive visibility
189: Frame.with(f -> f.width(widthSignal))         // reactive sizing, layout included
190: ```
191: 
192: The **raw form is sugar for a constant signal**; a **non-constant** signal
193: becomes a **node-level binding** — a change re-emits only that node's `SET_TEXT`
194: / `SET_PROPERTY`, and a constant emits as a plain property with **zero binding
195: overhead**. This holds for *every* value member, layout included
196: (`spacing`, `alignment`, `padding`, `frame`, `columns`, …): anything describable
197: in the protocol can animate. A control's two-way *value* takes a
198: `WritableSignal<T>`; every other member takes a one-way `Signal<T>`.

901: ### 5.6 Custom modifiers (developer-authored)
902: 
903: In SwiftUI any developer can define a modifier that applies to **any** existing
904: view — and Pathland is the same. This is a **first-class, MUST** property of
905: every conformant DSL: modifiers are never hard-bound to a view type.
906: 
907: - **Applicable to any view.** A modifier works on a library primitive
908:   (`Text`), a container (`VStack`), a control (`Button`), a custom view, or an
909:   already-modified view. The same modifier value applies everywhere.
910: - **One mechanism.** Core and application-authored modifiers are the **same
911:   surface**: a `ViewModifier` value applied via `.modifiers(...)`. There is
912:   **no per-modifier sugar on the view type**; a parameterized modifier is
913:   constructed with `Modifier.with(...)` and single-value modifiers pass the
914:   value directly ([§5.0](#50-authoring-a-modifier)).
915: 
916: | | Canonical | Java DSL (`com.pathland.view`) | Rust DSL (`pathland-view`) |

918: | authoring | `struct Card: ViewModifier { func body(content: Content) -> some View }` | `@FunctionalInterface ViewModifier { View body(View content) }` | `trait ViewModifier { fn apply(&mut Node) }` |

920: | single-value | `.modifier(Padding(16))` | `content.modifiers(Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16)))` | `content.modifiers(Padding(16.0))` |

925: 
926: **Emission contract**: a custom modifier composed from core modifiers emits the
927: same one-`SET_PROPERTY`-per-property deltas as writing the modifiers inline;
928: emission stays diff-based, and a renderer that cannot apply a modifier
929: **allows and ignores** it.
930: 
931: **Realization deltas**:
932: - **Rust** — every core modifier (`Padding`, `FontSize`, `ForegroundStyle`,

content.text:
All confirmed. The inventory is complete — the root cause is the leftover `View.with(ViewModifier...)` default on the `View` interface itself, which several call sites (including PlayerBar) are using. Here's the plan.

## Plan: ban `.with(...)` for modifiers — `modifiers(...)` is the only modifier operation

### Root fix (`pathland-view` library)
1. **`View.java`** — replace `default View with(ViewModifier...)` (the general modifier chain, View.java:61-72) with:
   `default View modifiers(ViewModifier...)` — same innermost-first body, returning `View`. Update the javadoc (lines 17-18, 61-72) to say the modifier operation is `.modifiers(...)`, never `.with(...)`. A plain `View` value (a probe, `config.label()`, a `Color`, a `FitSlot`) gets `.modifiers(...)`; `ViewBuilder.modifiers(...)` (ViewBuilder.java:40) already returns the builder, so it covariant-overrides the new interface default automatically.
2. **`BorderedButtonStyle.java:66`** — `config.label().with(...)` → `config.label().modifiers(...)`.
3. **`Label.java:109`** — `content.with(AccessibilityLabel.with(...))` → `content.modifiers(...)`.

### Call sites (demo + server + tests) — `.with(Modifier...)` → `.modifiers(...)`
- `MusicPlayerView.java:110-112` — **PlayerBar** `.with(Border..., Shadow...)` → `.modifiers(Border..., Shadow...)` (this is the reported case).
- `MusicPlayerView.java:118` — `.with(Clipped.with())` → `.modifiers(Clipped.with())`.
- `MusicPlayerView.java:125-127` — SizeThatFits `.with(Frame..., AccessibilityRole...)` → `.modifiers(...)`.
- `ColorSection.java:40` — `accent.get().with(Frame...)` → `.modifiers(...)`.
- `PathlandSession.java:132` — `app.newRoot().with(EnvironmentBinding...)` → `.modifiers(...)`.
- Tests: `SplitNavDemoTest.java:52`, `RouterTest.java:487/489, 626, 721`, `LabelTest.java:187` — same rename.

### Docs
4. **`pathland-view/status.md`** — it already claims the `View.with(ViewModifier...)` general chain is removed (line 41-42); reword so it now states `.modifiers(...)` is the one modifier operation and plain views use the interface default (drop the "in favor of" ambiguity). Update the demo file's class javadoc if it references `with(...)` for modifiers.

### Verify
5. `cd lib/java && mvn -o test` — full reactor green (currently 494). Confirm no `.with(ViewModifier...)` remains: `grep -rn "\.with(Border|Shadow|Frame|Clipped|AccessibilityRole|EnvironmentBinding|.*Style\.INSTANCE"` over `lib/java` yields nothing.

**Scope check**: `EnvironmentValues.with(key, value)` (Environment.java) is unrelated (a different type) and stays. `subscribe().with(...)` (Quarkus reactive) is unrelated. This aligns `View` with the spec's "three operations" (§1: `with`=values, `modifiers`, `children`).

Shall I proceed?

You're right — no more second-guessing. One decision needed, and I'll ask it directly:

The conflict: Java forbids a class from having a **static** method and an inherited **instance** method with the same signature. My change added `default View.modifiers(ViewModifier...)` on the `View` interface (required so a bare `View` value — `config.label()`, a `Color`, a probe — can apply modifiers). But every one of the 39 concrete view classes (`Text`, `VStack`, `Divider`, …) also declares a **static** `X.modifiers(...)` *first-call entry point* — that's the collision.

Only one can survive. My recommendation:

**Remove the static `X.modifiers(...)` first-call entry points** (all 39). `.modifiers(...)` becomes the single, instance-only modifier operation (interface default for bare views + the `ViewBuilder.modifiers` override for chains). Static call sites (`Divider.modifiers(...)`, `Spacer.modifiers()`, `Rectangle.modifiers(...)`, `VStack.modifiers(...)` in tests) become `Divider.with().modifiers(...)` etc. Update the DSL.md §2 note that says "Java holds the three statically on the view class" to reflect that modifiers is chainable/instance-only (values `with` and `children` stay static entry points).

The alternative — keeping the statics and dropping the interface default — is a non-starter because bare `View` values would have no way to apply modifiers.
